destinations.name: Goa
destinations.description: Goa is a vibrant seaside haven that allures tourists from every corner of the world. Its charm lies in its variety—golden beaches, thrilling water sports, ancient forts, easy-going vibe, and mouth-watering cuisine. Whether you’re after a serene escape, daring adventures, or rich cultural vibes, Goa greets you with open arms. It’s more than a coastal retreat; it’s an experience of life itself. The rhythm of its waves, aroma of spices, tunes of local music, and smiles of its people will steal your heart. To discover this enchanting coastal land, check our Goa tour packages.
tips: ATMs : ATMs can be easily found in most remote villages areas.
Credit Cards : Credit cards are commonly used in towns, but seldom in rural zones.
Bank : Banks are mainly located in major cities and tourist centres.
Drinking : The permissible drinking age in Goa is officially 18 years.
Safest: People of Goa are admired for their friendliness and warmth.

accordions.title: About Goa
accordions.content: Goa, India’s smallest yet most vibrant state, is a tropical paradise known for its golden beaches, Portuguese heritage, lively nightlife, and laid-back charm. Nestled along the Arabian Sea on India’s western coast, Goa blends Indian and European influences seamlessly, reflected in its architecture, cuisine, and culture. Whether you’re drawn to the bustling energy of North Goa or the serene landscapes of South Goa, this coastal haven offers something for everyone — from adventure seekers and nature lovers to spiritual travellers and honeymooners. With palm-fringed beaches, ancient churches, spice plantations, and vibrant markets, Goa captures the true essence of relaxation and celebration.

accordions.title: Top 5 Reasons to Book Goa Tour Packages
accordions.content: Diverse Beaches: Enjoy pristine sands and blue waters at famous beaches like Baga, Calangute, Palolem, and Colva — each offering a different vibe.Cultural Heritage: Discover centuries-old churches, forts, and temples that narrate Goa’s fascinating history under Portuguese influence.Adventure and Water Sports: Experience thrilling activities like parasailing, scuba diving, jet-skiing, and banana boat rides.Nightlife and Music: From beach parties to nightclubs like Tito’s and Mambo’s, Goa never sleeps when it comes to entertainment.Gastronomic Delights: Relish a unique mix of Indian and Portuguese cuisine, especially seafood dishes and spicy Goan curries.

accordions.title: Things to Do in Different Seasons
accordions.content: Winter (November to February): The best time to visit for beach activities, water sports, and festivals like Sunburn and Christmas. Enjoy pleasant weather and lively nightlife.Summer (March to May): Ideal for quieter vacations with fewer crowds. Take advantage of off-season discounts and visit waterfalls or spice farms.Monsoon (June to September): A time to experience Goa’s lush greenery, romantic rains, and cultural festivals like Sao Joao. Perfect for nature photography and peaceful retreats.

accordions.title: Best Places to Visit in Goa
accordions.content: Beaches: Baga, Anjuna, Morjim, and Palolem for sunbathing, music, and water sports.Heritage Sites: Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral, and Chapora Fort for history enthusiasts.Nature Escapes: Dudhsagar Waterfalls and Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary for adventure seekers.Cultural Towns: Panjim and Old Goa, where art galleries, churches, and colorful Portuguese villas await.Spiritual Spots: Shantadurga Temple and Mangueshi Temple showcasing Goa’s Hindu traditions.

accordions.title: Unique Experiences of Goa
accordions.content: Cruise along the Mandovi River during sunset or enjoy a backwater tour.Visit spice plantations to learn about Goa’s agrarian traditions.Participate in beach yoga and wellness retreats.Join vibrant local festivals like Carnival or Shigmo to experience Goan spirit.Take a heritage walk through Latin Quarter (Fontainhas) to admire its colonial charm.

accordions.title: Shopping in Goa
accordions.content: Shopping in Goa is a colorful affair. From street bazaars to designer boutiques, you’ll find everything from handmade jewelry to bohemian clothing. The Anjuna Flea Market and Mapusa Market are perfect for souvenirs, beachwear, handicrafts, and antiques. Don’t miss local cashew nuts, feni (local spirit), and Goan spices, ideal mementos of your trip.

accordions.title: Food and Cuisine of Goa
accordions.content: Goan cuisine is a delicious blend of Indian, Portuguese, and coastal flavors. Must-try dishes include Goan Fish Curry, Vindaloo, Xacuti, and Prawn Balchão. Vegetarians can savor local specialties like Mushroom Xacuti and Bebinca, a layered dessert. Street food like Ros Omelet and Poi (local bread) offer authentic local taste. Seafood lovers will be delighted by the freshness and spices that define Goan cooking.

accordions.title: Art and Culture of Goa
accordions.content: Goa’s art and culture are a vivid reflection of its colonial history and traditional Indian roots. The state hosts numerous music festivals, art exhibitions, and folk performances. Dance forms like Fugdi, Dekhni, and Dhalo highlight the region’s folk traditions, while Fado music and Latin-inspired art showcase its Portuguese influence. Local craftsmanship thrives in pottery, shell art, and bamboo work. The annual Goa Carnival and International Film Festival of India further celebrate Goa’s creative and cosmopolitan spirit, making it one of India’s most culturally diverse destinations.

destinations.name: Bali
destinations.description: Hailed as The Island of the Gods, Bali is one of more than 17,000 islands in Indonesia. What truly sets it apart from the rest is the affection and admiration it receives from visitors across the globe. With a population of around 4.37 million, Bali offers an endless list of experiences that make it a dream holiday destination — all waiting to be explored when you book one of our Bali tour packages.
tips: ATMs can be found easily only in select locations.
Credit cards are commonly accepted everywhere.
Smooth banking experience awaits in Bali.
Bali’s legal drinking age is set at 18.
The Balinese are known for their warm hospitality.
Bali observes a unique weekend: Friday and Saturday.

accordions.title: About Bali
accordions.content: Bali is a tropical paradise that perfectly balances lush natural beauty with deep cultural roots. Known worldwide as The Island of the Gods, it features majestic volcanoes, emerald rice terraces, and pristine beaches that invite relaxation and adventure in equal measure. The island’s spiritual heart beats through its countless temples, daily offerings, and vibrant festivals, creating a charm that’s hard to resist. Whether you’re chasing sun-kissed shores, rich traditions, or thrilling adventures, Bali offers an experience unlike any other.

accordions.title: Essential Tips To Know Before Travelling To Bali
accordions.content: Before visiting Bali, it’s important to know a few essentials. The local currency is the Indonesian Rupiah, and while ATMs are widely available in popular areas, it’s best to carry some cash for rural spots. Dress modestly when visiting temples and always wear a sarong if required. Bargaining in markets is expected, but do it politely. The island follows Hindu traditions, so respect local customs and ceremonies. Traffic can be busy, so factor in travel time when planning your days. Lastly, bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect both your skin and Bali’s delicate marine life.

accordions.title: Bali At A Glance
accordions.content: Country: IndonesiaPopulation: Approximately 4.37 millionKnown for: Beaches, temples, rice terraces, and vibrant cultureMain City: DenpasarPopular Areas: Ubud, Seminyak, Kuta, Nusa Dua, CangguClimate: Tropical, with warm weather year-roundLanguages: Indonesian (Bahasa), Balinese, and English in tourist zones

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit Bali
accordions.content: Breathtaking Beaches – From white sands in Nusa Dua to surfer’s paradise in Uluwatu.Rich Culture – Traditional dances, ancient temples, and art villages.Adventure Activities – Diving, trekking, rafting, and volcano hikes.Wellness Retreats – Yoga studios and world-class spas for ultimate relaxation.Exotic Cuisine – A mix of Indonesian flavours with international fusion.

accordions.title: Best Time To Visit Bali
accordions.content: Bali is a year-round destination, but the dry season from April to October is perfect for outdoor adventures, beach days, and water sports. The wet season from November to March sees fewer crowds and lower prices, making it ideal for budget travellers. Cultural events like Galungan and Nyepi offer unique festival experiences if you time your visit right.

accordions.title: Top Things To Do In Bali
accordions.content: Watch the sunset at Tanah Lot Temple.Explore the terraced fields of Tegallalang in Ubud.Snorkel or dive in Menjangan Island.Climb Mount Batur for a sunrise trek.Attend a Balinese cooking class.Relax in a luxury beach club in Seminyak.

accordions.title: Shopping In Bali
accordions.content: Bali is a treasure trove for shoppers. Browse traditional markets in Ubud for handmade crafts, paintings, and silver jewellery. Seminyak offers chic boutiques and designer stores, while Kuta is perfect for budget-friendly finds. Don’t miss Sukawati Art Market for colourful textiles and souvenirs. Remember — bargaining is part of the fun!

accordions.title: Art And Culture In Bali
accordions.content: Bali’s art scene is as rich as its landscapes. Villages like Ubud are hubs for painters, sculptors, and dancers who preserve traditional techniques while embracing modern influences. Daily offerings, temple ceremonies, and festivals like the Bali Arts Festival showcase the island’s deep spiritual roots. Every corner tells a story, from intricately carved temple gates to shadow puppet performances.

accordions.title: Foods To Try Out In Bali
accordions.content: Nasi Goreng – Indonesia’s signature fried rice.Babi Guling – Traditional roasted suckling pig.Lawar – A mix of vegetables, coconut, and minced meat.Sate Lilit – Minced seafood satay wrapped around lemongrass sticks.Dadar Gulung – Sweet green pancakes filled with coconut and palm sugar.Pair your meals with tropical fruits like mangosteen, rambutan, and salak (snake fruit).

Whether you’re traveling for leisure, business, or a mix of both, Dubai promises an experience like no other.

accordions.title: About Dubai
accordions.content: Dubai, the crown jewel of the United Arab Emirates, is a city that blends futuristic innovation with deep-rooted traditions. Famous for its record-breaking skyscrapers, man-made islands, luxury shopping malls, and world-class attractions, Dubai has become one of the most visited cities in the world. What makes Dubai extraordinary is its ability to offer everything—golden deserts, pristine beaches, cultural heritage, extravagant nightlife, and family-friendly entertainment—all in one destination. Whether you’re traveling for leisure, business, or a mix of both, Dubai promises an experience like no other.

accordions.title: Essential Tips To Know Before Travelling To Dubai
accordions.content: Before heading to Dubai, keep these tips in mind for a smooth journey:Visa Requirements: Depending on your nationality, you may need a tourist visa. Many countries are eligible for on-arrival visas.Cultural Etiquette: Dubai is cosmopolitan yet respectful of its Islamic roots. Dress modestly in public, and avoid public displays of affection.Transportation: The Dubai Metro is modern and convenient, while taxis and ride-hailing apps are widely available. Renting a car is also an option for exploring beyond the city.Currency: The official currency is the UAE Dirham (AED), and both cash and credit cards are accepted everywhere.Laws: Alcohol is allowed only in licensed venues, and it’s important to avoid smoking or eating in public during Ramadan fasting hours.Planning with these tips ensures a hassle-free holiday while respecting local customs.

accordions.title: Dubai At A Glance
accordions.content: Country: United Arab EmiratesCapital: Abu Dhabi (Dubai is the most populous city)Population: Over 3 million, with a large expatriate communityLanguage: Arabic (English is widely used for business and tourism)Currency: Dirham (AED)Time Zone: GMT +4Dubai is a multicultural city, home to more than 200 nationalities, making it one of the most diverse cities in the world.

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit Dubai
accordions.content: Iconic Landmarks: Marvel at Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world, and the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab.Desert Adventures: Experience dune bashing, camel riding, and traditional desert camps under starry skies.Luxury & Shopping: From designer boutiques in Dubai Mall to bargains at Gold and Spice Souks, shopping is world-class.Family-Friendly Entertainment: Theme parks like IMG Worlds of Adventure, Aquaventure Waterpark, and Dubai Parks and Resorts keep families entertained.Blend of Cultures: Dubai embraces modernity while preserving Emirati traditions, offering travelers a unique cultural mix.

accordions.title: Best Time To Visit Dubai
accordions.content: The ideal time to visit Dubai is between November and March, when the weather is pleasant and outdoor activities are enjoyable. This period is also marked by major events like the Dubai Shopping Festival and New Year celebrations, making it the peak tourist season. Summers (June to September) are extremely hot, but many attractions are indoors, allowing visitors to enjoy malls, aquariums, and indoor ski slopes comfortably. If you want fewer crowds and good hotel deals, late spring and early autumn are great options.

accordions.title: Top Things To Do In Dubai
accordions.content: Climb the Burj Khalifa: Witness panoramic views of the city from its observation decks.Dubai Fountain Show: Watch the world’s largest choreographed fountain dance to music.Desert Safari: An adventure with dune bashing, sandboarding, camel rides, and cultural shows.Dhow Cruise: Sail through Dubai Marina or Dubai Creek while enjoying dinner and entertainment.Water Adventures: Try jet skiing, parasailing, and diving in the Arabian Gulf.Entertainment Parks: Enjoy thrilling rides at Motiongate, Legoland, or Wild Wadi Water Park.

accordions.title: Top Places To Visit In Dubai
accordions.content: Burj Khalifa: The tallest tower with breathtaking observation decks.The Dubai Mall: A mega shopping complex with 1,200+ shops, an aquarium, and indoor ice rink.Palm Jumeirah: A stunning man-made island with luxury resorts and beach clubs.Dubai Marina: A vibrant waterfront lined with skyscrapers, cafes, and restaurants.Dubai Frame: An architectural marvel offering views of old and new Dubai.Global Village: A cultural and entertainment hub showcasing pavilions from around the world.Al Fahidi Historical District: A glimpse into Dubai’s heritage with museums and traditional wind-tower houses.

accordions.title: Shopping In Dubai
accordions.content: Shopping in Dubai is nothing less than an extravaganza. Modern malls like The Dubai Mall and Mall of the Emirates house international brands, luxury boutiques, and entertainment centers. Traditional markets (souks) such as the Gold Souk, Spice Souk, and Textile Souk offer authentic Emirati shopping experiences. Bargaining is common in local markets, while malls offer fixed prices. Don’t miss the Dubai Shopping Festival, a month-long extravaganza featuring unbeatable discounts, raffles, and cultural events.

accordions.title: Shopping in Croatia
accordions.content: Croatia offers a blend of traditional and modern shopping experiences:Local Markets: Zagreb Dolac Market and Split Green Market offer fresh produce, cheeses, and handicrafts.Souvenir Shops: Pick up handcrafted lavender products, lacework, and olive oil.Fashion Boutiques: Designer brands and local Croatian designers in major cities.Jewelry & Art: Unique pieces inspired by Croatian history and landscapes are widely available.

accordions.title: What To Eat In Dubai?
accordions.content: Dubai’s food scene is a paradise for food lovers, offering everything from traditional Emirati dishes to international cuisine. Some must-try local dishes include:Al Harees: A slow-cooked wheat and meat dish, popular during Ramadan.Al Machboos: A spiced rice dish with meat or seafood.Shawarma: A Middle Eastern favorite with grilled meat wrapped in bread.Luqaimat: Sweet fried dumplings drizzled with date syrup.Beyond local flavors, Dubai is home to celebrity-chef restaurants, Michelin-starred dining, and global street food, making it a true culinary capital.

destinations.name: Manali
destinations.description: Manali, nestled in the lap of the majestic Himalayas, is one of India’s most beloved hill stations, attracting travelers throughout the year. Located in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh, this charming town sits gracefully along the banks of the Beas River. Known for its snow-covered peaks, lush pine forests, apple orchards, and vibrant markets, Manali serves as a gateway to adventure, spirituality, and natural beauty. Whether you’re a honeymooner seeking serenity, an adventurer craving mountain thrills, or a traveler searching for peace, Manali offers something for everyone. From ancient temples and serene monasteries to thrilling treks and paragliding adventures, Manali truly captures the magic of the mountains.
tips: ATMs  : ATMs are easily found in Manali, but uncommon in remote villages.
Credit Cards : Credit cards are generally accepted across most parts of Manali.
Bank : Banks are present throughout Manali, though limited in outer villages.
Drinking : The permitted legal drinking age within Manali is 18 years.
Safest : Locals of Manali are well-known for their warm and friendly hospitality.

accordions.title: About Manali
accordions.content: Manali, nestled in the lap of the majestic Himalayas, is one of India’s most beloved hill stations, attracting travelers throughout the year. Located in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh, this charming town sits gracefully along the banks of the Beas River. Known for its snow-covered peaks, lush pine forests, apple orchards, and vibrant markets, Manali serves as a gateway to adventure, spirituality, and natural beauty. Whether you’re a honeymooner seeking serenity, an adventurer craving mountain thrills, or a traveler searching for peace, Manali offers something for everyone. From ancient temples and serene monasteries to thrilling treks and paragliding adventures, Manali truly captures the magic of the mountains.

accordions.title: Manali At A Glance
accordions.content: Manali is a delightful mix of tranquility and thrill, offering experiences that range from cultural exploration to outdoor adventure. It’s a destination where nature meets spirituality, and every corner unveils breathtaking scenery.Location: Kullu Valley, Himachal Pradesh, IndiaAltitude: Approximately 2,050 meters above sea levelClimate: Cool summers and snowy wintersBest Known For: Snow sports, nature trails, temples, and romantic getawaysLanguages Spoken: Hindi, English, and PahariNearest Airport: Bhuntar Airport (about 50 km away)Ideal Trip Duration: 4 to 6 daysFamous Spots: Solang Valley, Rohtang Pass, Old Manali, Hidimba Temple

accordions.title: Essential Tips to Plan a Trip to Manali
accordions.content: Best Season Choice: Visit between October and February for snow or March to June for pleasant weather and outdoor activities.Accommodation: Book hotels or homestays in advance during peak seasons like summer and winter holidays.Packing Essentials: Carry warm clothes year-round as temperatures drop sharply at night, especially in higher altitudes.Travel Routes: Manali is accessible via road from Delhi and Chandigarh; private cabs, buses, and self-drive options are popular.Altitude Sickness: While not very common in Manali itself, visitors traveling to higher points like Rohtang Pass should stay hydrated and avoid heavy exertion.Local Transport: Rent scooters, bikes, or hire taxis to explore nearby attractions conveniently.Permits: Visitors heading to Rohtang Pass require special permits; these can be applied for online.Sustainable Travel: Carry reusable water bottles, avoid littering, and respect the fragile mountain ecosystem.

accordions.title: Top Reasons to Visit Manali
accordions.content: Adventure Sports: Experience paragliding, skiing, zorbing, river rafting, and trekking across the majestic valleys.Romantic Getaways: Perfect for couples, Manali offers cozy cottages, mountain views, and peaceful riverside retreats.Snow Experience: Rohtang Pass and Solang Valley offer breathtaking snow views and winter sports.Spiritual Vibes: Ancient temples like Hidimba Devi Temple and Manu Temple provide a touch of divine calm.Scenic Beauty: Verdant forests, roaring rivers, and blooming meadows make Manali a photographer’s paradise.Cultural Richness: Encounter Himachali traditions, local festivals, and handmade crafts in the Old Manali markets.Gateway to Leh-Ladakh: Manali is the starting point for one of the world’s most thrilling road journeys — the Manali-Leh Highway.

accordions.title: Best Places to Visit in Manali
accordions.content: Solang Valley: A hotspot for adventure sports and winter snow activities.Rohtang Pass: Known for its snow-covered terrain and panoramic mountain views (accessible seasonally).Old Manali: Famous for its bohemian cafes, charming guesthouses, and relaxed vibe.Hidimba Devi Temple: A 16th-century wooden temple surrounded by deodar forests, dedicated to Goddess Hidimba.Manu Temple: Believed to be the abode of Sage Manu, offering peace and panoramic views.Vashisht Village: Known for its natural hot springs and ancient stone temples.Jogini Waterfall: A scenic short trek from Vashisht, perfect for nature lovers.Nehru Kund: A natural spring believed to be linked to Pandava legends.Mall Road: The bustling heart of Manali filled with shops, cafes, and local handicrafts.Van Vihar: A serene park ideal for leisurely walks amid tall deodar trees.

accordions.title: Famous Hot Springs in Manali
accordions.content: Manali is home to several natural hot springs known for their healing and therapeutic properties:Vashisht Hot Springs: Located in Vashisht Village, these sulphur springs are believed to cure skin ailments and relax muscles.Kalath Hot Springs: Found on the way to Manikaran, they are popular among locals for their soothing warmth.Manikaran Hot Springs: Situated near Kullu, this site holds religious significance for both Hindus and Sikhs. The springs here are so hot that food is sometimes cooked directly in the water!These hot springs not only provide physical relief but also a sense of spiritual rejuvenation amid the tranquil Himalayas.

accordions.title: Best Time to Visit Manali
accordions.content: Each season offers its own charm, making Manali an all-year-round destination, depending on what kind of experience you seek.Summer (March–June): Ideal for sightseeing, trekking, and paragliding. Pleasant temperatures make it perfect for outdoor exploration.Monsoon (July–September): The region experiences moderate rainfall, bringing lush greenery but occasional landslides—recommended for nature photographers.Winter (October–February): A wonderland of snow! Ideal for honeymooners and adventure lovers seeking skiing or snowboarding experiences.

accordions.title: Shopping in Manali
accordions.content: Shopping in Manali is a delightful mix of local art, culture, and craftsmanship. The Mall Road and Old Manali Market are filled with stalls offering Himachali shawls, woolen caps, handmade jewelry, Tibetan prayer wheels, and wooden handicrafts. The Tibetan Market is a great place to buy souvenirs like thangkas and Buddhist artifacts. Don’t miss the Bhuttico Shawl Factory in Kullu for authentic Pashmina and Kullu shawls. Local fruit wines, jams, and dry fruits also make perfect take-home gifts. Bargaining is common, so shop with a friendly smile and patience.

accordions.title: Food and Cuisine of Manali
accordions.content: Manali’s cuisine reflects the warmth and simplicity of mountain life, blending Himachali and Tibetan flavors.Siddu: A steamed bread stuffed with walnuts or poppy seeds, served with ghee.Thukpa: A Tibetan noodle soup, perfect for cold evenings.Momos: Steamed dumplings filled with vegetables or meat, found at every corner.Dham: A traditional Himachali feast served during festivals, made with lentils, rice, and yogurt curry.Trout Fish: Locally sourced from Beas River, a must-try for seafood lovers.Tibetan Bread and Butter Tea: Staple comfort foods often enjoyed in local homes and cafes.Cafes in Old Manali, such as Café 1947 and Drifters’ Inn, offer international cuisine with stunning mountain views, making dining an experience in itself.

accordions.title: Art and Culture of Manali
accordions.content: Manali’s culture is a vibrant tapestry of Himachali traditions and Tibetan influences. The locals, known for their warm hospitality, celebrate festivals like Kullu Dussehra, Losar, and Winter Carnival with music, dance, and colorful attire. Traditional folk music accompanied by instruments like nagara and dholak is integral to every celebration. Handicrafts such as wool weaving, metalwork, and wooden carvings showcase the artistic talent of the region. Buddhist monasteries and Hindu temples coexist harmoniously, reflecting the area’s spiritual diversity. Visitors can also explore local art galleries and cultural centers to witness Manali’s creative side come alive.

accordions.title: About Kerala
accordions.content: Kerala, fondly called “God’s Own Country,” is a coastal paradise in southern India, known for its lush greenery, tranquil backwaters, serene beaches, and rich cultural heritage. Nestled between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, Kerala offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, wildlife, and vibrant traditions. From the spice-laden hills of Wayanad to the palm-lined shores of Kovalam, Kerala captivates every traveler with its diversity and charm.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: Kerala is famous for its backwaters, especially in Alappuzha and Kumarakom.The state is a hub for Ayurvedic treatments and wellness retreats.Traditional festivals like Onam and Thrissur Pooram showcase Kerala’s vibrant culture.Houseboat cruises and elephant sanctuaries are major attractions.The state boasts one of the highest literacy rates in India.

accordions.title: Essential Tips to Plan a Trip to Kerala
accordions.content: Transportation: Kerala is well-connected via Cochin and Trivandrum airports; trains and buses connect major towns.Accommodation: Options range from luxury resorts and houseboats to budget homestays.Clothing: Light cotton clothes are ideal; carry a raincoat during monsoon season.Local Etiquette: Respect local customs, especially in temples and religious sites.Health: Try Ayurvedic massages, but drink only bottled water and eat from trusted eateries.

accordions.title: Top 5 Reasons to Visit Kerala
accordions.content: Backwaters and Houseboats: A unique experience cruising through serene canals in Alappuzha and Kumarakom.Hill Stations and Tea Gardens: Explore the scenic beauty of Munnar and Wayanad.Wildlife and Nature: Encounter exotic species at Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary and Silent Valley National Park.Culture and Festivals: Traditional art forms like Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and vibrant festivals.Cuisine and Spices: Savor authentic Kerala dishes, rich in coconut, spices, and seafood.

accordions.title: Best Time to Visit Kerala

destinations.name: Switzerland
destinations.description: Switzerland is often called the “Land of the Alps,” but there’s more to it than just mountains. It is one of the few countries with four official languages—German, French, Italian, and Romansh. Despite its small size, Switzerland is home to over 1,500 lakes, including Lake Geneva and Lake Lucerne. The country is famous for its neutrality, having avoided direct involvement in wars for centuries. Switzerland also produces some of the world’s finest chocolates and luxury watches, and the Swiss consume more chocolate per person than any other nation. Interestingly, the country does not have a president in the traditional sense—its government is run by a Federal Council of seven members who share leadership equally.

destinations.name: Africa
destinations.description: The origin of the name Africa has intrigued historians for centuries. While there is no single agreed-upon explanation, many scholars trace its earliest use back to the Romans, who referred to the lands around present-day Tunisia and Northern Algeria as “Africa.” Others suggest the term could have come from the Greek word a-phrike, which means “without cold,” reflecting the continent’s generally warm climate. An alternative theory connects the name to the ancient Egyptian phrase afru-ika, translating to “motherland.” These varying theories only deepen the rich historical tapestry of Africa.
destinations.climate: Many people hold the misconception that Africa is a culturally homogenous continent. However, one of the most fascinating truths about Africa is its remarkable ethnic and linguistic diversity. The continent is home to over 3,000 tribes, such as the Zulu, Bantu, Berber, and Maasai. These communities collectively speak more than 2,000 languages, including Arabic in the north, Zulu in the south, and French across many West African nations like Mali, Senegal, and Benin. This cultural richness is what makes exploring Africa an unforgettable experience through our carefully crafted Africa tour packages.

accordions.title: About Africa
accordions.content: The origin of the name Africa has intrigued historians for centuries. While there is no single agreed-upon explanation, many scholars trace its earliest use back to the Romans, who referred to the lands around present-day Tunisia and Northern Algeria as “Africa.” Others suggest the term could have come from the Greek word a-phrike, which means “without cold,” reflecting the continent’s generally warm climate. An alternative theory connects the name to the ancient Egyptian phrase afru-ika, translating to “motherland.” These varying theories only deepen the rich historical tapestry of Africa.Many people hold the misconception that Africa is a culturally homogenous continent. However, one of the most fascinating truths about Africa is its remarkable ethnic and linguistic diversity. The continent is home to over 3,000 tribes, such as the Zulu, Bantu, Berber, and Maasai. These communities collectively speak more than 2,000 languages, including Arabic in the north, Zulu in the south, and French across many West African nations like Mali, Senegal, and Benin. This cultural richness is what makes exploring Africa an unforgettable experience through our carefully crafted Africa tour packages.Geographically, Africa is equally awe-inspiring. It is a land of striking contrasts and vast ecosystems. The Sahara Desert, the largest hot desert in the world, stretches across 31% of the continent. In contrast, savannahs—home to iconic wildlife like lions, elephants, and giraffes—make up about 46% of the landmass. Meanwhile, the lush and biodiverse Congo Basin rainforest spans roughly 12% of Africa. This vital ecological zone extends across nine countries, including the Democratic Republic of Congo, Republic of Congo, Central African Republic, Cameroon, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, and Zambia.Whether you're interested in ancient history, tribal cultures, or awe-inspiring landscapes, our Africa tour packages are designed to take you deep into the heart of the continent. Learn more about Africa as you journey through its deserts, rainforests, and savannahs, each offering a glimpse into the continent's unmatched natural beauty and vibrant heritage.

accordions.title: Africa is categorized into five subregions by the United Nations.
accordions.content: Northern Africa – A Blend of Desert, Culture, and Coastal CharmNorthern Africa comprises six Arab nations: Morocco, Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, and Sudan. Arabic is widely spoken here, and Islam is the predominant religion. Bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the west, the Mediterranean Sea to the north, and the Arabian Plate to the east, the region serves as a cultural and historical bridge between Africa and the Middle East. Egypt, uniquely, spans two continents—Africa and Asia—via the Sinai Peninsula. Our Africa tour packages offer enriching experiences in Northern Africa, highlighting its ancient cities, Islamic architecture, and desert landscapes.Eastern Africa – Vibrant Cultures and Rapid GrowthEastern Africa, part of Sub-Saharan Africa, includes a diverse list of countries: Burundi, Comoros, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Rwanda, Seychelles, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Territories like Reunion Island and Mayotte also fall under this region. Known as the continent’s fastest-growing area, nations like Kenya and Tanzania have made significant economic strides in recent years. With our Africa tour packages, travelers can witness the Great Rift Valley, Mount Kilimanjaro, serene beaches, and rich tribal heritage.Middle Africa – Heart of the Continent and the Congo BasinMiddle Africa, another Sub-Saharan zone, features countries like Angola, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and São Tomé and Príncipe. Dominated by the vast Congo Basin, this area is home to the second-largest tropical rainforest on Earth. The equator runs through many of these nations, contributing to their tropical climate. Explore pristine rainforests, river systems, and rich biodiversity with our specially designed Africa tour packages for Middle Africa.Southern Africa – Land of Wildlife, Minerals, and Scenic BeautySouthern Africa encompasses Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa, Eswatini (formerly Swaziland), Zambia, and Zimbabwe. This region is renowned for its expansive savannahs, abundant wildlife, and scenic landmarks like Victoria Falls and the Kalahari Desert. Mineral wealth—including diamonds, gold, and platinum—adds to its global significance. Our Africa tour packages showcase everything from thrilling safaris to cultural tours and scenic drives along South Africa’s Garden Route.Western Africa – Rich in Culture, Yet Economically ChallengedWestern Africa includes nations such as Benin, Burkina Faso, Cape Verde, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, and Togo. Although this region faces economic hardship, it is rich in cultural traditions, natural resources, and historical significance. Islam is the dominant religion, especially in the northern areas. Our Africa tour packages to West Africa dive deep into its musical heritage, colorful festivals, and coastal charm.

accordions.title: Top Reasons to Explore Africa
accordions.content:
From breathtaking wildlife safaris and stunning natural landscapes to centuries-old history and vibrant cultures, Africa is a continent that promises endless exploration. With such a wide variety of experiences across its 54 countries, Africa tour packages are the perfect way to uncover the continent’s unmatched beauty and depth. If you're searching for a one-of-a-kind travel destination, here’s why Africa should be at the top of your list.Breathtaking Wildlife ExperiencesIf you've ever been captivated by David Attenborough’s legendary wildlife documentaries showcasing the Maasai Mara or the sweeping African savannahs, then exploring Africa in person is the ultimate bucket-list experience. Nowhere else on Earth offers such an extraordinary variety of wildlife in one place. Africa is home to more than one million animal species, including over 1,000 types of mammals, 2,600 species of birds, and more than 3,000 species of fish.From the elephant, the world's heaviest land animal, to the giraffe, the tallest, and the cheetah, the fastest—Africa proudly hosts nature’s most iconic species. Through our expertly designed Africa tour packages, you can witness the awe-inspiring Great Migration in Kenya and Tanzania, swim alongside whale sharks in Zanzibar, observe the magical sight of sea turtles hatching along the East African coastline, and embark on gorilla trekking expeditions deep in the lush jungles of Uganda, Rwanda, and the Congo.



	Wildlife ExperienceLocation




	The Great Wildebeest MigrationSerengeti (Tanzania), Masai Mara (Kenya)


	The Annual Zebra MigrationKalahari Desert (Botswana)


	Hatching of Sea TurtlesEast Coast of Africa – Kenya, Tanzania, Eritrea, Mozambique, Madagascar


	Gorilla TrekkingCongo Basin – Uganda, Congo, Rwanda


	Staying with GiraffesGiraffe Manor (Kenya)


	Big Five SightingsSouth Africa, Tanzania, Botswana, Kenya, Namibia, Rwanda, Zambia, Zimbabwe


	Conservation VolunteeringUsangu Expedition Camp (Tanzania), Marataba Conservation Camp (South Africa)


	Swimming with DugongsBazaruto Archipelago (Mozambique)



FoodThe vast continent of Africa offers a variety of dishes, ranging from tagines of North Africa to the savoury stews and flatbreads of East Africa to the barbecues of Southern Africa. You must visit Africa to sample the colourful one-pot jollof rice in West African countries like Nigeria and Ghana, flatbreads like injera and dholl puri in East African countries like Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Mauritius, the unique carbs like fufu, ugali, and deep-fried plantains.African cuisine has also been influenced by immigrants who settled here over time. Indian influences include sambusas, chapatis, bunny chow, and pakoras. In addition to the Arabs, Ottomans, and colonials, Italians have influenced African cuisine, especially in Libya, Somalia, Ethiopia, and Eritrea.Some popular dishes on the continent include falafel, tagine, jollof rice, injera, boerewors, egusi soup, and fufuAdventureWith such dramatic landscapes, it’s only natural that Africa offers unlimited adventure opportunities. You can go trekking in the Congo Basin rainforests in Rwanda and Uganda, trek through the Sahara Desert, enjoy watersports in Mauritius and Seychelles, go hot air balloon ride above the Masai Mara, or join your friends for a whitewater rafting adventure in the Zambezi River. Lake Malawi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its extensive fish species and is also a renowned watersport destination offering snorkelling, scuba diving, kayaking, sailing, and wakeboarding.Some popular adventure activities you can enjoy in your Africa tour package include:



	AdventureLocations




	TrekkingMount Kilimanjaro, Mount Kenya, Rim of Africa Trail


	Gorilla TrekkingBwindi National Park, Mgahinga Gorilla National Park, Volcanoes National Park


	Whitewater RaftingNile River (Uganda), Zambezi River (Zambia & Zimbabwe), Fish River Canyon (Namibia)


	Big Game Walking SafarisSouth & North Luangwa National Parks, Kruger National Park, Mana Pools National Park


	Bungee JumpingBloukrans Bridge (South Africa), Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe)



HistoryWhile wildlife is a big tourist attraction, Africa also has a rich cultural heritage and history. After all, Africa is the birthplace of human civilisation! From the pyramids and temples of Egypt and the Roman buildings of Morocco to the great ruins of Zimbabwe and Carthage, there is much to explore and experience in Africa. The Cradle of Humankind is a paleoanthropological site famous for its fossils of some of the earliest earthly inhabitants, including hominids, our distant human like ancestors. Famous among these are Mrs Ples and Little Foot, the latter being a complete hominid skeleton and the former being a pre-human skull that dates back more than 2 million years.

accordions.title: Geographical Facts About Africa
accordions.content: Africa is the second-largest and the second-most populous continent.It is home to the largest river in the world the NileThe equator divides Africa into two almost equal halves.Africa is called Mother Continent as it is the oldest inhabited continent.Africa is the only continent that crosses all 3 lines of latitude: the Tropic of Cancer, the Tropic of Capricorn, and the Equator.The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.The Congo Basin is the world’s second-largest rainforest.Many areas of Africa receive snow Drakensberg, Mount Kilimanjaro, Mount Kenya, TunisiaThe Great Wildebeest Migration is the largest & longest animal migration in the worldCoffee supposedly originated in EthiopiaAfrica is slowly splitting into two through the East African Rift System that runs through Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.The Sahara Desert was once a tropical rainforest.Africa has 30% of the world’s mineral reserves rich in cobalt, platinum, manganese, chromium, and bauxite.Africa is home to the heaviest (elephant), largest bird (ostrich), the largest frog (Goliath frog) and the fastest animal (leopard) in the world.Africa produces 70% of the world’s cocoa beans.

accordions.title: Cultural Facts About Africa
accordions.content: Africa is home to over 3000 different ethnicities speaking more than 2000 languagesThe evil eye is a familiar concept across Africa. The evil eye pendant, or nazar pendant, is believed to have originated in Egypt.Africans were the first to go on fishing expeditions; harpoons, daggers & other tools said to be over 90,000 years old have been found in Congo.Africans were the first miners; a 43,000 year old mine was discovered in Eswatini (erstwhile Swaziland).Pyramids aren’t specific to Egypt alone you can find them in Libya, Algeria, Sudan, and Nigeria. The Nubian pyramids (Sudan) are older than Egyptian pyramids.Mali was one of the wealthiest ancient empires. Mansa Musa, the Mali King, is believed to be the wealthiest man to have ever lived.Africans are pioneers of astronomy; the 7000 year old Nabta Playa stones help track summer solstice & are the oldest known astronomical site.Maize is the most common source of starch in Africa. It goes by different names across the continent: ugali, sadza, nsima, chima, bugali, sokoro, pap, etc.The Maasai people participate in adult, a practice where men jump high to show social status and even attract potential brides.The Mursi women wear lip plates, i.e., they insert wooden plates in their lips to symbolise beauty and social status.Christianity & Islam are the major religions in Africa. While North Africans predominantly practice Islam, Christianity is predominant in Southern Africa.

accordions.title: Most Visited Countries In Africa
accordions.content: Egypt (11.7 Million)Egypt is a major tourist destination in Northern Africa, attracting tourists for its pyramids, ancient Egyptian ruins, and historic cities like Alexandria, Cairo, and Giza. It was ruled by several empires, including the Achaemenids, Romans, and Ottomans, who built beautiful buildings and temples. Tourists visit Egypt to explore its beautiful architecture, including the pyramids of Giza, the Valley of the Kings, the Luxor and Karnak temples, and the Abu Simbel complex. Remember to include a Nile cruise on your African tour packages itinerary if you visit this beautiful country.Morocco (10.9 Million)Morocco has always enamoured tourists with its ancient cities, Islamic architecture, beautiful handicrafts, and delectable cuisine. The Sahara Desert is another popular attraction, with activities like buggy riding, desert safari, and dune hiking. Famous cities like Fez, Casablanca, Marrakech, Chefchaouen, Tangier, and Meknes. Morocco’s souks are equally famous for their spices, argan oil, tea, shoes, and ceramicware. Remember to visit Morocco’s popular attractions like Jardin Majorelle, Bahia Palace, and the Ouzuod Waterfalls with our Africa tour packages. Tunisia (6.4 Million)Tunisia is famed for its balmy beaches along the Mediterranean Coast and its historic cities like Carthage, Hammamet, and Mahdia. Some of Tunisia’s Medinas or old towns are legendary with their colourful markets, palaces, alleys, fountains, and small craft workshops. If you’d like to explore ancient Roman ruins without the crowd and the hassle of Rome, Tunisia is the place to visit. The Roman amphitheatre in El Jem is the largest outside of Italy. For instance, Carthage, one of the wealthiest cities in the ancient Mediterranean, was once home to over 700,000 people. Some of its famous ruins include the Baths of Antoninus, Roman Theatre, ancient Roman houses and statues.South Africa (3.51 Million)From beautiful beaches and wildlife safaris to delectable food and wine tours, there are plenty of reasons to visit South Africa. The country is called Rainbow Nation because of its multicultural ethos, including multiple religions, ethnicities, and languages. The weather is equally pleasant, with sensational summers and mild winters. South Africa is also home to prehistoric fossils, including skeletons of early humanoids, aptly called The Cradle of Human Civilisation. For those interested in apartheid history, we recommend visiting Robben Island, where Nelson Mandela spent several years in prison. Call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334) for a detailed Africa tour packages itinerary. Algeria (2.9 Million)Algeria has a varied landscape, with the northern part of the Mediterranean and the southern part encompassing the Sahara Desert. The country also has beautiful Roman archaeological sites in Timgad, Djemila, and Tipaza. The cuisine is another popular attraction with flavourful dishes like tagine, couscous, and brik. If you’re planning a stress-free beach vacation, Algeria is the perfect destination with Tipasa Beach, Ain El Turck Beach, and Sidi Fredj.The Sahara Desert is popular for desert safaris, camel rides, and dune bashing. If you’d like to include Algeria in your Africa tour packages itinerary, Call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334)

accordions.title: Least Visited Countries In Africa
accordions.content: Equatorial GuineaEquatorial Guinea is an unexplored paradise surrounded by jungles, pristine beaches, and abundant wildlife. There are hundreds of plant and animal species endemic to the country, including island bronze naped pigeon and the annobon paradise flycatcher. While it is popular among adventure tourists, poor marketing and infrastructure, corrupt government, and a lack of medical care make it impossible to visit Equatorial Guinea. Obtaining a tourist visa is an equal nightmare.Sao Tome & PrincipeMorocco has always enamoured tourists with its ancient cities, Islamic architecture, beautiful handicrafts, and delectable cuisine. The Sahara Desert is another popular attraction, with activities like buggy riding, desert safari, and dune hiking. Famous cities like Fez, Casablanca, Marrakech, Chefchaouen, Tangier, and Meknes. Morocco’s souks are equally famous for their spices, argan oil, tea, shoes, and ceramicware. Remember to visit Morocco’s popular attractions like Jardin Majorelle, Bahia Palace, and the Ouzuod Waterfalls with our Africa tour packages. ComorosComoros is an island country in East Africa located between Mozambique and Madagascar. It comprises three islands: Grand Comore, Moheli, and Anjouan. The country is famous for its beaches, mountains, and abundant marine life, including sea turtles, corals, humpback whales, and dolphins. It is one of the very few places where you’ll find lemurs outside of Madagascar. While it is indeed beautiful, Comoros isn’t a preferred tourist destination because of its remoteness and insecure political climate.MauritaniaMauritania was once a French colony and the only meeting point between Maghreb and Sun-Saharan Africa. Given its location, the country is famous for its ancient ruins, such as Chinguetti. If you are a nature lover, Parc National du Banc d’Arguin is one of the best places for birdwatching in Africa. Despite its abundant wildlife and ancient ruins, not many people visit Mauritania because of terrorism and safety risks. The country is also prone to infectious diseases like cholera, measles and tuberculosis.

accordions.title: 5 Must Visit Countries In Africa
accordions.content: With 54 countries in the continent, it’s natural that you cannot restrict your travel to just the popular destinations. Here’s a list of must-visit places you must include in your Africa tour package itinerary.ZimbabweThis is one of Africa’s less-visited countries but is packed with spectacular experiences, including Victoria Falls, one of the world’s largest waterfalls. It is also home to amazing wildlife sanctuaries, including the Hwange National Park and the Matoba National Park. The Great Zimbabwe is a UNESCO World Heritage Site that was once the home of the Queen of Sheba. Zimbabwe is one of the best places to see the Big Five. Check out our Zimbabwe tour packages if you’d like to explore the country. TanzaniaTanzania is a beautiful country famous for its wildlife safaris, Mount Kilimanjaro, and historical places like Olduvai Gorge Museum. It is also the best place to witness the Great Wildebeest Migration, when millions of wildebeest cross the plains of the Serengeti. Head to Zanzibar to explore Tanzania’s pristine beaches. It is also called Spice Island, thanks to the many Persians, Chinese, and Arab traders who have sailed through Zanzibar’s harbour. If you’d like to explore the local indigenous culture, don’t miss a stay with the Maasai people.Kenya

accordions.title: Most Visited Tourist Attractions Included In Our Africa Tour Packages
accordions.content: With its beautiful geography, abundant wildlife, and cultural heritage, Africa is a blessed continent that offers tourists a wholesome experience. Africa is home to some of the best wildlife safaris, gorgeous beaches, prehistoric artefacts, and even ski resorts. Here’s a list of tourist attractions you must include in your Africa tour packages.Serengeti National ParkThe Serengeti is a UNESCO World Heritage site thanks to the Great Wildebeest Migration, where millions of wildebeests migrate searching for fresh pastures and water. Its rich biodiversity allows tourists to observe the Big Five from close quarters, ensuring an unforgettable safari experience. In addition to the Big Five, the national park is home to millions of ungulates, leopards, cheetahs, and several bird species. Call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334) to include a safari on your Africa tour package itinerary.Victoria FallsVictoria Falls is the largest waterfall in the world – almost twice the height of Niagara Falls in North America. It is located on the border of two countries – Zambia and Zimbabwe. The local name for Victoria Falls is Mosi-Oa-Tunya, or smoke that thunders, which refers to the huge roar and misty spray that resembles smoke. Victoria Falls is considered one of the seven wonders of the natural world and is always included in our Africa tour packages itinerary. Masai Mara National ReserveThe Masai Mara is located in Southwest Kenya and is famous for its scenic savannah plains and abundant wildlife, including the Big Five. Other animals you can observe at the Masai Mara include wildebeest, giraffe, zebra, and cheetah. The reserve gets its name from its original inhabitants, the Masai people. You can spend a night observing animals from close quarters, watching wildebeests from a hot air balloon, going on a game drive, or spending time with the locals in their village.Mount KilimanjaroLocated in Tanzania, Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa’s tallest mountain and the largest free-standing mountain in the world. It probably gets its name from the Swahili word for mountain, kilim, and the KiChagga word for whiteness the mountain is famed for its snow-capped peak. The mountain is a popular hiking spot because the trail is relatively easy and does not require as much equipment or experience. While the glaciers are believed to be over 11,000 years old, environmental changes are causing the glaciers to retreat.Kruger National ParkThe Kruger National Park is the largest in Africa and the oldest in South Africa. Besides the Big Five, you can observe a range of animals from close quarters, including the African wild dog, warthogs, spotted hyenas, wildebeest, and the vervet monkey. With our Africa tour packages, you can stay in one of the many hotels near the park and enjoy a full-day safari or a guided park tour or go hiking, walking, and backpacking. Pyramids of GizaThe pyramids of Giza are a UNESCO World Heritage Monument and one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. These were originally tombs built for Egyptian pharaohs as they were believed to become gods in the afterlife. The Giza pyramids were built for Pharoah Khufu, his son Pharoah Khafre, and Khafre’s son, Menkuare. The materials to build the pyramid were shipped from across Egypt through the Nile. The tombs are invaluable as they describe everyday life in Egypt thousands of years ago.Abu SimbelRamesses II built the Abu Simbel temples on the west bank of the Nile River. The temples are carved out of a mountain and contain four giant statues of a seated Ramesses II. They were built so that on two days of the year, sunlight falls directly in the inner sanctuary. However, as a result of relocating the temples to their current site, the sun no longer shines in the inner sanctum. The smaller of the two temples is dedicated to Queen Nefertiti.

accordions.title: Popular Cities Included In Our Africa Tour Packages
accordions.content: Marrakech (Morocco)Marrakech is a colourful city famous for the medina, which hosts old souks, cafes, and art deco homes. The town probably gets its name from the Berber word murr akush or land of God. The city is only a few kilometres away from Toubkal, the highest peak in North Africa. Some iconic buildings in the city include the El Badi Palace, the Ben Youssef Madrasa, and La Jardin Majorelle. Don’t miss to sample Moroccan cuisine, especially the iconic mint tea. To include Marrakech to your Africa tour packages, call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334)Cape Town (South Africa)This is South Africa’s capital city and the country’s oldest city. Situated at the tip of the Cape Peninsula, the city is home to over 10 Blue Flag beaches, including Boulders Beach, where you can spot African penguins. Cape Town is also home to the famous Table Mountain, a flat-top mountain offering breathtaking views of the city. It is a popular hiking trail and is especially famous for providing the perfect backdrop to people looking to propose to their fiancés.Johannesburg (South Africa)Johannesburg is South Africa’s largest city, offering a perfect blend of traditional heritage and modern amenities. Some of its famous attractions include the Cradle of Humankind, Lion Park, the Johannesburg Zoo, the Johannesburg Botanical Garden, and Mandela House. You can also visit the local market in Soweto, grab a drink at one of Jo’burg’s rooftop cafes, or try one of the many adventure sports offered in the city.Fez (Morocco)Fez is Morocco’s cultural capital and is famous for its Medina, now listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The monuments within the Medina include palaces, residences, mosques, and markets. The thousands of alleyways within the Medina are over 1000 years old, bearing witness to the city’s popularity that waxed and waned over the centuries. It is a car-free zone where tourists can travel by camel or walk by foot to observe the city’s historical buildings. Fez is also home to tanneries that date back almost 1000 years, the oldest in the world.Cairo (Egypt)Cairo is Egypt’s capital and is famous for its heritage, especially Islamic and military monuments. Because of its ancient history, the city is often called the cradle of civilisation, especially the pyramids of Giza. The longest river in the world, the Nile, flows through Cairo, which is probably why locals call it Umm al Dunya or the Mother of the World. Cairo is also home to the oldest university in Africa, the Al-Azhar University and the Babylon Citadel, an ancient fortress built in 30 BC.Nairobi (Kenya)Nairobi is Kenya’s capital and home to the famous Nairobi National Park. It is one of Africa’s fastest-growing cities. Besides its wildlife safaris, the city has a vibrant nightlife, including restaurants, pubs, and cafes. Within the city, you will also find traditional Kenyan villages or Bomas that showcase the life of the indigenous tribes. When in Nairobi, don’t miss Giraffe Manor, the most Instagrammed hotel in the world, where you can enjoy breakfast with giraffes and even feed them. To include the Giraffe Manor in your Africa tour packages, call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334)Alexandria (Egypt)Alexandria is Egypt’s second-largest city. It was established by Alexander the Great in 332 BC. He wanted the city to be the finest in the world, so it was for over 1,000 years, thanks to its strategic location between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. The beautiful Montazah Palace is another famous attraction that now houses a museum. Visit the famous beaches of Al-Ma’moura, Mandara, and Al-Assafrah, dotted with beautiful seafront boulevardsCasablanca (Morocco)Casablanca is a modern city that is very unlike the rest of Morocco. Some of its iconic attractions include the Hassan II Mosque and the Church of Notre Dame of Lourdes. The Casablanca Festival and Jazzablanca are some of its famous festivals. The Medina in Casablanca is equally historic and established since 15 BC.

accordions.title: Shopping
accordions.content: Given the huge diversity of cultures, it’s only natural that Africa offers plenty of shopping options. Northern African countries like Morocco, Egypt, Algeria, and Tunisia are famous for their carpets and rugs, while beadwork is famous in Sub-Saharan countries like Kenya, Tanzania, Ghana, Nigeria, and South Africa. The souks of Morroco and Egypt are also famous for their leather products, ceramicware, and spices.Call us at (+91 99404 63566 / +91 73973 56334) for a detailed shopping experience included in our Africa tour packages.Nigeria is famous for its handcrafted wooden facemasks, handstitched leather purses, and indigo-dyed cloth produced by Yoruba women. Kenya is renowned for their soapstone carvings, Maasai beads, masks, ebony carvings, and kitengala glass.If you visit Tanzania, remember to buy Maasai crafts like jewellery, wood carvings, and Tanzanian coffee. Ethiopia is also famous for its coffee, with locals believing it originated there. Straw baskets, honey, wickerware, and clay pottery are also common handicrafts in Ethiopia.When in Madagascar, remember to buy their prized vanilla and vanilla-infused products. Baobab-themed souvenirs like oil and powder are also popular.South Africa is famous for its batik fabrics, beaded jewellery, pewter cutlery, and handmade silk. You can also buy handwoven textiles, wooden masks, sculptures, and pottery.Mauritius is famous for its dodo souvenirs and the fabled Mauritius rum. When in Seychelles, don’t forget to buy spices, tea, vanilla, and perfumes made from locally sourced ingredients like ylang ylang and coco de mer.As for where to buy these products, local African markets are the best place to shop for souvenirs. However, tourists need to exercise caution when purchasing from local shopkeepers. For instance, shopkeepers in the old souks in Morocco and Egypt will likely quote ten or twenty times the original price. In contrast, a local seller in Tanzania will likely even quote even double the actual price.Call us or send a message on Instagram for a customised Africa tour package.

accordions.title: Food
accordions.content:
The Africans were among the first to practice agriculture, cultivating millet, yams, sorghum, and oil palms since 3000 BCE. In fact, parts of North Africa, including the Nile Delta, were part of the Fertile Crescent, i.e., regions where the first settled agricultural communities settled. They also domesticated cattle, sheep, and donkeys over 7000 years ago or earlier. Given its vast geography, it is natural that the food is diverse and inspired by the local climate and landscape.For instance, beef is rarely eaten in East Africa, where cattle are revered and even used as currency by some tribes, including the Maasai and Samburu. But beef is a common protein in North Africa and is used to make koftas and kebabs. Central Africans are traditionally hunter-gatherers, hunting exotic animals like baboons and warthogs for meat. Today, the diet includes cassava, plantains, yams, and sweet potatoes as the main starch, which are eaten with stews made using peanuts, chicken, beef, and okra.West African cuisine incorporates rice, millet, and cassava as starches. Popular dishes include jollof rice and fufu, which are eaten with a spicy stew called egusi soup. Goat, chicken, and beef are common protein sources. Black-eye peas are another common ingredient in Western Africa, where they are added to stews and ground to make fritters and porridge.Southern African cuisine is a blend of various influences, including Portuguese, British, Indian, Malay, and Dutch. Barbecue is a huge part of the cuisine in this region and called braai. Beef and chicken are common protein staples, but game meat like antelope, crocodile, and ostrich are also common.Seafood is a common ingredient in most regions, especially Western Africa. It is often included in stews and is also smoked. In fact, smoked fish is even given as dowry by some tribes. Smoked prawns are ground and added to soups for added flavour and even form a main ingredient in shitto, a spicy sauce in Ghana.Religious practices and historical trade with other regions also influenced African cuisine. For instance, in some native religions like Ifa, Bukongo, and Vodun, food is considered spiritual medicine, and ethically butchering an animal is considered an important aspect of a priestess’s learning. Cardamom seeds and cloves are a staple of Ethiopian cuisine and East African cuisine in general, thanks to the influence of trade from India and the Arab countries.Berbere is another unique spice blend that gets its name from the Berber people and probably originated in Ethiopia.Similarly, sacrifice is an essential aspect of Islamic African cuisine on Eid-Al-Adha. Cow, lamb, camel, goat, etc., were the common sacrificial animals.Communal eating is common in many African countries, including Ethiopia, Mali, Eritrea, Ghana, and Nigeria. Injera is a common bread across Ethiopia and Eritrea and is often served on a plate upon which the gravy is placed.As for cooking medium, ghee is a common fat used in East Africa, while West Africans predominantly use palm oil for their cooking and religious practices. In the North African countries of Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, and Egypt, olive oil is commonly used, while ghee and sesame oil are widely used in Sudan.

destinations.name: South America
destinations.description: Experience South America with luxury handpicked accommodations, private chauffeured transfers, and comprehensive guided sightseeing curated by TripbyGenie specialists.
tips: The Amazon River, at 7,062 km, ranks as the second-longest river globally.
The Andes stretch 7,000 km across South American nations.
The Rio Carnival draws millions of global visitors each year.
Colombia boasts shores on both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.
Pink River Dolphins are found only in the Amazon River.
The Amazon hosts over 7,000 distinct butterfly species.

accordions.title: Geographical Facts about South America
accordions.content: The Andes Mountains form the longest continental mountain range on Earth.The Amazon Rainforest spans across nine countries and houses 10% of the world’s known species.Lake Titicaca, between Peru and Bolivia, is the highest navigable lake in the world.Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest non-polar desert on the planet.The Iguazu Falls, shared by Argentina and Brazil, is one of the largest and most spectacular waterfall systems in the world.

accordions.title: Cultural Facts about South America
accordions.content: South America has over 400 indigenous languages still spoken today.Music and dance like tango (Argentina), samba (Brazil), and cumbia (Colombia) are vital cultural expressions.Catholicism remains the dominant religion, influenced by colonial history.South America is known for colorful festivals, often blending indigenous and colonial traditions.Many South American cultures value strong family ties and communal celebrations.

accordions.title: Most Visited Countries in South America (2023)
accordions.content: Brazil – Known for Rio de Janeiro, the Amazon, and cultural festivals.Argentina – Attracts visitors with Patagonia, Buenos Aires, and wine regions.Colombia – Gaining popularity for its coastlines, heritage cities, and biodiversity.Peru – A top destination for Machu Picchu and Incan history.Chile – Known for diverse landscapes from the Atacama to Torres del Paine.

accordions.title: Most Popular Cities in South America
accordions.content: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil – Beaches, Christ the Redeemer, and Carnival.Buenos Aires, Argentina – Tango, steak, and colonial architecture.Lima, Peru – Gateway to Machu Picchu and a top culinary destination.Bogotá, Colombia – A high-altitude capital known for art and history.Santiago, Chile – A vibrant mix of modern life and Andean views.

accordions.title: Most Visited Tourist Attractions in South America
accordions.content: Machu Picchu, (Peru) – Iconic Incan citadel in the Andes.Christ the Redeemer, (Brazil) – Towering statue overlooking Rio.Iguazu Falls, (Argentina/Brazil) – One of the world’s most stunning waterfalls.Salar de Uyuni, (Bolivia) – World’s largest salt flat with surreal landscapes.Galápagos Islands, (Ecuador) – A haven for wildlife and ecological wonders.

accordions.title: Least Visited Countries in South America (2023)
accordions.content: Guyana – Though rich in eco-tourism, it's still off the radar for many.Suriname – Offers rainforests and colonial architecture but sees fewer tourists.Paraguay – Lacks major international tourism marketing but offers cultural depth.Bolivia – Despite its natural beauty, it remains under-visited compared to neighbors.French Guiana – A French territory with unique charm, yet low tourist numbers.

accordions.title: Most Notable Festivals in South America
accordions.content: Rio Carnival (Brazil) – The world’s largest carnival celebration.Inti Raymi (Peru) – Festival of the Sun, honoring Incan heritage.Carnaval de Barranquilla (Colombia) – Second-largest carnival in South America.Fiesta de la Vendimia (Argentina) – Celebrates the grape harvest in Mendoza.Tapati Festival (Easter Island/Chile) – Rich in Polynesian and Chilean traditions.

accordions.title: Common Etiquette to Remember When Visiting South American Countries
accordions.content: Greetings matter – A handshake or cheek kiss is common in many countries.Respect personal space – But note that physical closeness may be more accepted.Dress modestly – Especially in religious or rural areas.Punctuality varies – Some countries operate on relaxed time.Learn basic phrases – Spanish or Portuguese greetings are appreciated.

accordions.title: Common Must-Try Delicacies in South America
accordions.content: Arepas (Colombia/Venezuela) – Cornmeal cakes filled with cheese or meats.Feijoada (Brazil) – A rich black bean stew with pork.Ceviche (Peru) – Raw fish marinated in citrus, served with onions and chili.Empanadas (Argentina/Chile) – Pastry stuffed with savory fillings.Churrasco (Brazil) – A barbecue tradition with endless grilled meats.

tips: ATMs are readily available in urban areas but may be scarce in rural regions.
Most establishments across Canada accept major credit cards.
In Canadian cities, locating a bank is generally straightforward and convenient.
The legal drinking age depends on the province—either 18 or 19 years old.
Canadians are widely recognized for their welcoming nature and warm hospitality.

accordions.title: About Canada
accordions.content: Canada, the second-largest country in the world, is a land of stunning contrasts—from towering mountain ranges and glacial lakes to vibrant multicultural cities and indigenous heritage. With ten provinces and three territories, it offers a diverse travel experience. Whether you're drawn to the scenic wilderness, French-infused charm of Quebec, or cosmopolitan life in cities like Toronto and Vancouver, Canada is a destination that never disappoints.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: Canada has two official languages: English and French.It's home to over two million lakes—more than any other country.The maple leaf is a national symbol and is featured on the flag.The country spans six time zones.Canadians are known for politeness, punctuality, and love for nature.

accordions.title: Things to Remember Before Booking Tour Packages
accordions.content: Ensure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your travel date.Check visa requirements and processing times.Plan your itinerary according to the season—some attractions are seasonal.Book accommodations early during peak travel periods.Travel insurance is highly recommended.Include both urban and nature-based activities in your plan.

accordions.title: Our Best Canada Tour Packages
accordions.content: Discover tailor-made Canada tour packages designed for every type of traveler—honeymooners, families, nature enthusiasts, and adventure seekers. accordions.content: Capital: OttawaCurrency: Canadian Dollar (CAD)Time Zones: Ranges from UTC -3.5 to UTC -8Major Cities: Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, CalgaryOfficial Languages: English and FrenchClimate: Varies by region—cold winters and mild summersTop Landmarks: CN Tower, Niagara Falls, Lake Louise, Parliament Hill

accordions.title: Shopping
accordions.content: From luxury brands to artisan markets, Canada offers diverse shopping experiences.Where to Shop: Toronto’s Eaton Centre, Vancouver’s Robson Street, and Montreal’s underground mallsWhat to Buy: Maple syrup, Canadian wine, indigenous crafts, ice wine, winter wearTax Info: Look out for duty-free options and keep receipts for tax refunds when eligible

accordions.title: Art and Culture
accordions.content: Canada is home to vibrant arts, music, and indigenous cultures.Explore art galleries like the National Gallery of CanadaAttend festivals such as the Toronto International Film Festival and Calgary StampedeLearn about First Nations through museums and cultural centersEnjoy live music, street performances, and local theater across cities

destinations.name: Central America
destinations.description: Costa Rica leads as the most visited country in Central America, attracting millions with its eco-tourism, wildlife reserves, and adventure activities. National parks like Manuel Antonio and Arenal Volcano remain top draws.
destinations.climate: Dress modestly when visiting rural communities or religious sites.
tips: Pacuare River in Costa Rica provides exciting rafting.
San Salvador Cathedral carries cultural and historic value.
Panama Canal links oceans—Atlantic to Pacific—a marvel.
Central America joins continents, edged by two oceans.
Coffee, bananas, pineapples—Central America's key exports.

accordions.title: Geographical Facts About Central America
accordions.content: The Pacuare River in Costa Rica offers world-class white-water rafting amidst tropical jungles.The Panama Canal serves as a crucial shipping route connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, revolutionizing global trade.Central America is flanked by the Pacific Ocean on one side and the Caribbean Sea on the other, forming a natural bridge between two continents.The region features a mix of volcanic mountains, lowland rainforests, highland plateaus, and extensive coastlines.Countries in the region export crops like coffee, bananas, and pineapples, supported by rich volcanic soil and tropical climates.

accordions.title: Cultural Facts About Central America
accordions.content: Central American culture blends indigenous traditions with Spanish colonial influences.Countries like Guatemala celebrate Maya heritage with traditional clothing, rituals, and languages.Music and dance are central to social life, with styles ranging from marimba in Guatemala to punto in Honduras.Handicrafts, such as woven textiles and wood carvings, are commonly found in local markets.Roman Catholicism remains dominant, though indigenous spiritual beliefs often merge with Christian practices.

accordions.title: Most Visited Country in Central America (2023)
accordions.content: Costa Rica leads as the most visited country in Central America, attracting millions with its eco-tourism, wildlife reserves, and adventure activities. National parks like Manuel Antonio and Arenal Volcano remain top draws.

accordions.title: Least Visited Countries in Central America (2023)
accordions.content: El Salvador and Nicaragua recorded the lowest tourist footfalls in 2023, largely due to political instability and limited tourism infrastructure—though they offer undiscovered beauty for off-the-beaten-path travelers.

accordions.title: Most Popular Cities in Central America
accordions.content: San José, Costa Rica – A hub for adventure tourism and cultural experiences.Panama City, Panama – A cosmopolitan capital known for the Panama Canal and modern skyline.Antigua, Guatemala – A UNESCO World Heritage Site with colonial charm and cobbled streets.Granada, Nicaragua – Famous for its colorful architecture and access to Lake Nicaragua.San Salvador, El Salvador – The country’s cultural and commercial heart, with historical sites and volcano views.

accordions.title: Most Visited Tourist Attractions in Central America
accordions.content: Panama Canal, Panama – A world engineering marvel.Arenal Volcano, Costa Rica – A scenic active volcano surrounded by hot springs.Tikal Ruins, Guatemala – Ancient Maya temples hidden in the jungle.Lake Atitlán, Guatemala – A stunning highland lake encircled by volcanoes and Mayan villages.Bay Islands, Honduras – Known for scuba diving and coral reefs.

accordions.title: Hidden Gems in Central America
accordions.content: Semuc Champey, Guatemala – Natural limestone pools in a remote jungle valley.Suchitoto, El Salvador – A colonial town known for art, festivals, and lake views.Ometepe Island, Nicaragua – Formed by twin volcanoes in Lake Nicaragua, ideal for hiking and eco-tourism.Tortuguero National Park, Costa Rica – Accessible only by boat or air, home to nesting sea turtles.Boquete, Panama – A cool highland town famous for coffee plantations and cloud forests.

accordions.title: Most Notable Festivals in Central America
accordions.content: Semana Santa (Holy Week) – Celebrated across the region with elaborate processions.Fiesta de Santiago, Nicaragua – Honoring Saint James with music, dancing, and bullfighting.Independence Day Celebrations – Held in mid-September in all countries, showcasing parades, cultural dances, and fireworks.Garífuna Settlement Day, Honduras – Celebrates the Afro-indigenous Garífuna culture with drumming, dancing, and storytelling.Dia de los Muertos, Guatemala – A colorful celebration honoring deceased loved ones, particularly in Santiago Sacatepéquez.

accordions.title: Common Etiquette to Remember When Visiting Central American Countries
accordions.content: Greet people with a handshake or a friendly “Buenos días” or “Buenas tardes.”Dress modestly when visiting rural communities or religious sites.Tipping around 10% is customary in restaurants and for tour guides.Avoid discussing politics or controversial topics unless invited to do so.Always ask before photographing locals, especially in indigenous areas.

accordions.title: Food in Central America
accordions.content: Gallo Pinto (rice and beans) – A staple in Costa Rica and Nicaragua.Pupusas – Thick corn tortillas filled with cheese, beans, or pork, famous in El Salvador.Tamales – Corn dough wrapped in banana leaves and steamed, enjoyed across the region.Ceviche – Marinated raw fish with lime juice, onions, and cilantro, popular in coastal areas.Tres Leches Cake – A sponge cake soaked in three types of milk, often served during celebrations.

destinations.name: Fiji
destinations.description: Fiji is a dream destination in the heart of the South Pacific, renowned for its crystal-clear waters and soft, golden sands. Whether you're an adventurer looking for action-packed days, a honeymooner seeking romance, or a solo traveler searching for tranquility, the Fiji Islands welcome all with open arms. Comprising 333 islands, this tropical paradise is celebrated for its scenic beaches, vibrant marine life, lush rainforests, and warm-hearted locals. From world-class diving spots and luxurious resorts to unique cultural traditions and stunning landscapes, a Fiji Islands tour package promises an unforgettable escape.
tips: Cash machines can be scarce in far-off places.
Remote spots might not accept plastic money.
Finding a bank can be tough in remote areas.
Fiji’s legal drinking age is set at twenty-one (21)
The people of Fiji are known for their kindness.

accordions.title: About Fiji
accordions.content: Fiji is an archipelago made up of over 330 islands, around 110 of which are inhabited. With a blend of Melanesian, Polynesian, Indian, and European influences, it offers a rich tapestry of cultures. The main islands—Viti Levu and Vanua Levu—house the majority of the population and are home to the capital city Suva and the popular resort town of Nadi.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: Currency: Fijian Dollar (FJD)Languages: English, Fijian, and HindiTime Zone: GMT+12Popular Islands: Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, Taveuni, Yasawa IslandsFun Fact: Fiji was one of the first countries to enter the new millennium!

accordions.title: India and Fiji Islands
accordions.content: India and Fiji share a strong historical and cultural connection. A large portion of Fiji’s population is of Indian descent, originally brought during the colonial era as indentured laborers. Today, Indo-Fijians contribute significantly to the nation’s culture, food, and festivals. Flights from India typically connect through Southeast Asia or Australia, and Indian travelers will feel welcomed by the familiar flavors and traditions found in many parts of Fiji.

accordions.content: Fijian cuisine is a delicious mix of native Pacific Islander flavors and Indian spices. Try traditional dishes like:Lovo: Food cooked underground on hot stonesKokoda: Raw fish marinated in coconut cream and limeFijian curry: Inspired by Indian flavors with a local twistCassava cake and taro dishes Fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and spicy chutneys are widely enjoyed.

accordions.content: Popular souvenirs include handmade shell jewelry, tapa cloth, wood carvings, and Fijian pearls. accordions.title: Art and Culture
accordions.content: Fijian culture is a blend of ancient traditions and modern expressions. Traditional dance (meke), tattooing, storytelling, and crafts like mat weaving are integral to village life. Cultural shows and firewalking ceremonies are often included in many Fiji Islands tour packages, providing an immersive experience of island heritage.
