destinations.name: Kolkata
destinations.description: If there is one destination in India that beautifully blends culture, cuisine, and charm, it is undoubtedly Kolkata. This fascinating city holds a rare balance—honoring its glorious past while embracing modern progress. The majestic colonial structures narrate its storied legacy, while sleek towers and bustling malls showcase its urban evolution. Narrow streets resound with cheerful chatter from tea stalls and lively coffee house debates, while upscale lounges and eateries offer a glimpse into the city’s vibrant nightlife. Kolkata is an experience that intertwines nostalgia with new energy, and you can explore its essence with our delightful Kolkata tour packages. Dive deep into the city’s art, heritage, food, attractions, and shopping delights to understand why the City of Joy continues to captivate every traveler’s heart.

accordions.title: About Kolkata
accordions.content: Kolkata, often called the “City of Joy,” is the cultural capital of India, known for its rich artistic heritage, colonial architecture, and intellectual vibrancy. Situated on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, it’s a city where every street corner tells a story of art, literature, and freedom. Kolkata beautifully fuses old-world charm with a contemporary pulse, offering travelers a perfect mix of tradition, modernity, and warmth.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: Once the capital of British India, Kolkata retains its colonial grandeur through its iconic buildings like the Victoria Memorial and Writers’ Building. It’s home to India’s oldest metro system, Asia’s first football club, and the famous Howrah Bridge. The city celebrates Durga Puja with unmatched fervor, and its people are known for their passion for literature, sweets, and football.

accordions.title: Essential Tips To Know Before Travelling To Kolkata
accordions.content: Language: Bengali is widely spoken, but English and Hindi are easily understood.Weather: Summers can be hot and humid; carry light cotton clothes.Transport: Use the Metro and app-based taxis for convenience.Safety: The city is generally safe, but stay alert in crowded markets.Local Etiquette: Respect religious customs and always remove shoes before entering temples.

accordions.title: Kolkata At A Glance
accordions.content: Location: Eastern India, along the Hooghly RiverPopulation: Over 4.5 million within city limitsFamous For: Durga Puja, sweets, colonial heritage, and literatureConnectivity: Well-connected by air, rail, and roadNickname: City of Joy

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit Kolkata
accordions.content: To witness the grandeur of Durga Puja celebrations.To explore architectural marvels like Marble Palace and Victoria Memorial.To experience Kolkata’s vibrant street food scene.To walk through the intellectual heart of India at College Street.To feel the warmth of locals and the charm of old-world lanes.

accordions.title: Best Time To Visit Kolkata
accordions.content: The ideal time to visit Kolkata is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant and the festive atmosphere is in full swing. Durga Puja, held around September–October, is the highlight of the year and showcases the city at its most beautiful.

accordions.title: Top Things To Do In Kolkata
accordions.content: Visit Howrah Bridge and take a ferry ride on the Hooghly River.Stroll through Park Street, the heart of nightlife and colonial cafés.Explore Indian Museum, one of the oldest museums in Asia.Attend a live theater performance or an art exhibition.Relax in Eco Park or take a heritage tram ride through the city.

accordions.title: Shopping In Kolkata
accordions.content: Kolkata offers a unique shopping experience, from local markets to upscale malls. New Market and Gariahat are famous for traditional saris, handicrafts, and accessories, while College Street is a paradise for book lovers. You can also find fine Bengali textiles, terracotta jewelry, and handmade souvenirs reflecting the city’s artistic spirit.

accordions.title: Dos and Don’ts While Travelling To Kolkata
accordions.content: DosDo try local Bengali sweets like rasgulla and sandesh.Do travel by tram for a nostalgic experience.Do carry cash for smaller shops and street vendors.Don’tsDon’t litter; keep the city clean.Don’t bargain aggressively in markets.Don’t photograph people without permission, especially at religious sites.

accordions.title: Best Quick Getaways From Kolkata
accordions.content: Sundarbans: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its mangrove forests and Bengal tigers.Shantiniketan: Tagore’s land of art and learning, rich in culture and serenity.Digha: A popular seaside town perfect for a weekend escape.Mandarmani: A quiet coastal retreat known for adventure activities.Bishnupur: Famous for terracotta temples and Baluchari sarees.

accordions.title: Foods To Try Out In Kolkata
accordions.content: Kolkata is a paradise for food lovers. Must-try dishes include kosha mangsho (spicy mutton curry), puchkas (pani puri), kathi rolls, and mishit doi (sweet yogurt). The city’s sweet shops, particularly those serving rosogolla and sandesh, are culinary landmarks in themselves.

accordions.title: Art And Culture In Kolkata
accordions.content: Art and culture thrive in every corner of Kolkata. The city is the birthplace of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore and home to vibrant art galleries, theaters, and music festivals. From the Academy of Fine Arts to Nandan, creativity flows endlessly here. Kolkata’s cultural calendar is filled with literary meets, film festivals, and traditional dance performances that celebrate both heritage and innovation.

destinations.name: Uttarakhand
destinations.description: Can you think of an Indian state that features snow peaks, sacred rivers, pilgrimage centers, and wildlife sanctuaries all together? Indeed, we can, and that beautiful state is Uttarakhand. Nestled in northern India, Uttarakhand is affectionately called ‘Dev Bhoomi’, meaning ‘Land of the Gods’. This sacred title comes from its abundance of holy places like Haridwar, Rishikesh, Kedarnath, and Badrinath. Besides its divine charm, Uttarakhand also boasts enchanting hill retreats such as Nainital, Auli, and Mussoorie, among many others. You can experience all these wonders and more through our Uttarakhand tour packages. Let’s take a journey through its culture, history, attractions, food, art, and shopping to understand why a visit here promises an unforgettable adventure.

accordions.title: About Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Uttarakhand, fondly known as the ‘Land of the Gods’ (Dev Bhoomi), is a stunning northern Indian state tucked away in the lap of the Himalayas. It is famous for its snow-clad peaks, sacred temples, lush valleys, and serene rivers. The state is divided into two regions—Kumaon and Garhwal, each offering distinct experiences in nature, spirituality, and adventure. From the divine charm of Kedarnath and Badrinath to the tranquil beauty of Nainital and Mussoorie, Uttarakhand captivates travelers with its unmatched blend of spirituality and scenic wonder.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: Capital: Dehradun (Winter) and Gairsain (Summer)Region: Northern IndiaLanguages Spoken: Hindi, Garhwali, Kumaoni, and EnglishFamous Rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Alaknanda, MandakiniMajor Hill Stations: Nainital, Mussoorie, Auli, LansdowneNicknames: Land of the Gods, Switzerland of IndiaNeighboring States: Himachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh

accordions.title: Essential Tips To Know Before Travelling To Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Carry Warm Clothes: Even during summer, nights can be chilly in the hills.Stay Hydrated: High altitudes can dehydrate you quickly—carry a water bottle.Respect Local Customs: Many places are sacred; dress modestly in temples and religious areas.Plan for Connectivity Issues: Internet and mobile networks may be weak in remote regions.Book Early During Peak Season: Summer and Char Dham Yatra periods see high tourist footfall.Travel Insurance: It’s advisable to have coverage for trekking or adventure sports.Avoid Plastic Use: Help preserve Uttarakhand’s fragile ecosystem by minimizing plastic waste.

accordions.title: Uttarakhand At A Glance
accordions.content: Location: Northern India, nestled in the HimalayasArea: Approximately 53,000 sq. kmBest Known For: Hill stations, pilgrimage sites, and adventure tourismClimate: Varies from subtropical in the valleys to alpine in the high mountainsMain Attractions: Rishikesh, Haridwar, Jim Corbett National Park, Mussoorie, Nainital, Auli, Kedarnath, Badrinath

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Spiritual Journeys: Visit sacred sites like Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri, part of the revered Char Dham circuit.Adventure Tourism: Enjoy thrilling activities such as river rafting in Rishikesh, skiing in Auli, and trekking to Valley of Flowers.Natural Beauty: Experience breathtaking mountain views, serene lakes, and lush forests.Wildlife Exploration: Spot tigers, elephants, and deer in Jim Corbett National Park, India’s oldest wildlife sanctuary.Cultural Richness: Immerse yourself in local fairs, traditional dances, and folk music.

accordions.title: Top Cities And Towns To Visit In Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Dehradun: The state capital surrounded by lush hills and home to the famous Robber’s Cave.Mussoorie: Known as the “Queen of Hills,” offering panoramic Himalayan views.Nainital: A charming hill town centered around the picturesque Naini Lake.Rishikesh: The Yoga Capital of the World and a hub for adventure sports.Haridwar: A sacred city where the Ganga flows pure and holy.Auli: Famous for skiing and panoramic Himalayan vistas.Almora: A serene town known for its culture, cuisine, and handicrafts.

accordions.title: Best Time To Visit Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Summer (March to June): Ideal for sightseeing, adventure, and pilgrimages.Monsoon (July to September): The landscape turns lush green but landslides can occur.Winter (October to February): Perfect for snowfall lovers and winter sports, especially in Auli and Mussoorie.For pilgrims, the Char Dham Yatra season usually begins in April/May and continues till October.

accordions.title: Top Things To Do In Uttarakhand
accordions.content: River Rafting in Rishikesh – Experience the thrill of the Ganges rapids.Wildlife Safari in Jim Corbett – Encounter Bengal tigers and exotic species.Trekking in Valley of Flowers – Witness a colorful paradise of alpine flora.Skiing in Auli – Glide over pristine snow-covered slopes.Boating in Naini Lake – Enjoy serene rides amid mountain reflections.Camping in Chopta – Sleep under the stars surrounded by forests.Yoga Retreats in Rishikesh – Rejuvenate with ancient wellness traditions.

accordions.title: Shopping In Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Shopping in Uttarakhand is a delightful experience blending tradition and nature. Local markets offer woollen garments, handmade candles, wooden crafts, and copperware.Nainital: Known for pine wood crafts and aromatic candles.Ranikhet: Offers handwoven woollen shawls and carpets.Haridwar: Famous for rudraksha beads, idols, and spiritual souvenirs.Dehradun: Renowned for its Basmati rice, local wines, and bakery products.

accordions.title: Dos and Don’ts While Travelling To Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Dos:Respect local traditions and temple rules.Keep the environment clean and use eco-friendly materials.Carry cash; ATMs may be limited in remote areas.Hire local guides for trekking and pilgrimages.Don’ts:Don’t litter or harm wildlife.Avoid alcohol or smoking near religious places.Refrain from taking risky shortcuts while trekking.Don’t disturb locals or photograph them without consent.

accordions.title: Foods To Try Out In Uttarakhand
accordions.content: The cuisine of Uttarakhand is simple, flavorful, and inspired by its hilly terrain. Must-try dishes include:Aloo Ke Gutke: Spicy potatoes served with puri and chutney.Kafuli: A spinach-based curry rich in nutrients.Bhatt Ki Churkani: A wholesome black soybean curry.Chainsoo: Made from roasted black gram dal.Arsa and Singori: Traditional sweets enjoyed during festivals.Pair these with a glass of Buransh (rhododendron) juice, a local specialty drink.

accordions.title: Art And Culture In Uttarakhand
accordions.content: Uttarakhand’s culture is deeply rooted in its spirituality, festivals, and folk traditions. The people are known for their warm hospitality and simplicity.Folk Dances: Langvir Nritya, Chholiya, and Jhora depict local legends.Music: Folk songs celebrate harvests, weddings, and nature.Festivals: Kumbh Mela, Ganga Dussehra, and Nanda Devi Raj Jat attract global attention.Craftsmanship: Wood carving, ringaal basketry, and wool weaving reflect the state’s artistic heritage.This vibrant culture, paired with serene landscapes, gives Uttarakhand its soulful charm and timeless allure.

destinations.name: South India
destinations.description: South India, also known as Peninsular India, is a land of diversity and deep cultural heritage. Encompassing the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, along with the union territories of Puducherry and Lakshadweep, this region is blessed with everything from pristine beaches and serene backwaters to lush forests and majestic temples. South India’s charm lies in its perfect blend of nature, spirituality, and tradition. Its rich history, classical music, artistic brilliance, and warm hospitality make it one of the most enchanting parts of the Indian subcontinent.

accordions.title: About South India
accordions.content: South India, also known as Peninsular India, is a land of diversity and deep cultural heritage. Encompassing the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, along with the union territories of Puducherry and Lakshadweep, this region is blessed with everything from pristine beaches and serene backwaters to lush forests and majestic temples. South India’s charm lies in its perfect blend of nature, spirituality, and tradition. Its rich history, classical music, artistic brilliance, and warm hospitality make it one of the most enchanting parts of the Indian subcontinent.

accordions.title: History Of South India
accordions.content: The history of South India dates back thousands of years, flourishing under powerful dynasties such as the Cholas, Cheras, Pandyas, and Vijayanagar rulers. These kingdoms left behind remarkable architectural wonders, including intricately carved temples, grand palaces, and ancient universities. South India’s maritime trade with Rome, Arabia, and Southeast Asia also shaped its culture and economy. From the temple towns of Madurai and Thanjavur to the forts of Karnataka and the colonial influences in Kochi and Chennai, the region’s past continues to live vividly through its monuments and traditions.

accordions.title: Tidbits
accordions.content: South India is home to more than 20 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, showcasing both cultural and natural significance.The region experiences diverse climates — tropical along the coasts and cooler in the hilly interiors.It is known for its classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, and Mohiniyattam.South India boasts some of the world’s oldest Dravidian languages, including Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, and Malayalam.The region’s coastline stretches for over 2,500 kilometres, offering numerous scenic beaches.

accordions.title: Things to Know Before Visiting South India
accordions.content: Before embarking on your journey through South India, it’s helpful to understand its seasonal variations. The best time to visit is between October and March, when the weather is pleasant. Respect local customs and dress modestly, especially while visiting temples and religious sites. South Indians are known for their hospitality and value politeness, so a warm greeting goes a long way. Carry light cotton clothing for the humid coastal areas and comfortable shoes for sightseeing. Also, be prepared to enjoy spicy cuisine and always keep yourself hydrated during the trip.

accordions.title: South India At A Glance
accordions.content: Capital cities: Chennai, Bengaluru, Thiruvananthapuram, Hyderabad, and AmaravatiLanguages: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, English, and HindiBest time to visit: October to MarchMajor attractions: Backwaters of Kerala, Hampi ruins, Mysore Palace, Marina Beach, Meenakshi Temple, and Coorg HillsPopular festivals: Pongal, Onam, Ugadi, Vishu, and DussehraFamous cuisine: Dosa, Idli, Appam, Hyderabadi Biryani, and Chettinad curry

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit South India Tour Packages
accordions.content: South India tour packages promise a complete experience — from heritage to adventure. The region’s peaceful beaches, verdant hill stations, and timeless temples make it a traveller’s paradise. History lovers can explore centuries-old ruins, while nature enthusiasts can unwind in Kerala’s houseboats or Coorg’s coffee estates. South India’s festivals, classical art forms, and Ayurveda traditions provide insight into its rich cultural fabric. Whether you’re seeking spiritual solace, scenic beauty, or culinary delights, South India offers a travel experience that’s deeply fulfilling and unforgettable.

accordions.title: Mouthwatering Cuisine
accordions.content: South Indian cuisine is a delicious journey of flavours, textures, and aromas. Each state adds its unique twist — Tamil Nadu is known for its spicy Chettinad dishes, Kerala delights with coconut-based curries, Karnataka offers Mysore masala dosa, while Andhra Pradesh serves fiery biryanis. The use of rice, lentils, tamarind, curry leaves, and spices creates a wholesome balance in every meal. Traditional breakfasts like idli, dosa, and vada are complemented by flavorful chutneys and sambar, while desserts like payasam and Mysore pak add a sweet ending to the feast.

accordions.title: Ayurveda Wellness Treats
accordions.content: South India, particularly Kerala, is the cradle of Ayurveda — the ancient Indian system of natural healing. Ayurvedic retreats and wellness centers offer rejuvenating therapies that detoxify the body and calm the mind. Treatments such as Panchakarma, herbal massages, and steam baths use time-tested methods to restore balance and vitality. Tourists can indulge in these holistic experiences in tranquil resorts nestled amidst coconut groves, backwaters, or hill ranges. These Ayurveda wellness treats are perfect for those seeking peace, relaxation, and a deeper connection between body and spirit.

accordions.title: Heritage Cities
accordions.content: South India’s heritage cities narrate tales of glory and devotion through their timeless monuments. Madurai is renowned for the majestic Meenakshi Amman Temple, while Thanjavur showcases Chola art and architecture. Mysore impresses with its royal palace and silk tradition, and Hampi reveals the grandeur of the Vijayanagar Empire through its stone-carved temples. Each city boasts unique architectural brilliance, traditional crafts, and vibrant local life. Exploring these heritage destinations lets you walk through centuries of living history still preserved in every stone and street.

accordions.title: Unique Art Forms
accordions.content: South India is a treasure trove of classical and folk art forms that have flourished for centuries. Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu, Kathakali and Mohiniyattam from Kerala, and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh represent the pinnacle of Indian dance traditions. The region also excels in traditional music, particularly Carnatic music, and in temple arts like Tanjore painting and intricate bronze sculpting. Folk performances such as Yakshagana, Theyam, and Karagattam showcase storytelling through rhythm and movement. These art forms not only entertain but also preserve the region’s spiritual and cultural legacy.

accordions.title: The Five States Of South India
accordions.content: Together, these five states create a mosaic of traditions, languages, and landscapes that make South India one of the most captivating travel destinations in the world.Tamil Nadu – Famous for its Dravidian temples, classical arts, and ancient heritage cities like Madurai and Thanjavur.Kerala – Known as “God’s Own Country,” it offers tranquil backwaters, lush greenery, and Ayurvedic wellness experiences.Karnataka – Home to the royal city of Mysore, the coffee plantations of Coorg, and the historic ruins of Hampi.Andhra Pradesh – Celebrated for its Tirupati temple, spicy cuisine, and cultural vibrancy.Telangana – A blend of Nizam’s grandeur and modern charm, best represented by Hyderabad’s iconic Charminar and delectable biryani.

destinations.name: West India
destinations.description: West India is a captivating region that offers a perfect fusion of history, heritage, adventure, and natural beauty. Encompassing the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, and parts of Rajasthan, this region showcases the essence of India’s vibrant spirit. From the golden sands of Goa’s beaches to the majestic forts of Rajasthan and the cultural richness of Gujarat, every corner tells a unique story. The region is also home to cosmopolitan cities like Mumbai and Pune that pulse with modern energy while retaining deep cultural roots. West India’s diverse landscapes — ranging from the Western Ghats to arid deserts — make it a year-round destination for travellers seeking both relaxation and exploration.

accordions.content: The weather varies widely — coastal regions are humid while inland areas can be hot or dry. Plan accordingly.Always carry sunscreen, sunglasses, and comfortable footwear for sightseeing.Try local transport like Mumbai’s local trains or Goa’s scooters for an authentic experience.Respect religious customs at temples and heritage sites.Keep some cash handy, as smaller towns may have limited digital payment options.Pre-book accommodations during festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi or Navratri, as demand soars.

accordions.title: West India At A Glance
accordions.content: West India is a melting pot of geography, culture, and tradition. Stretching from the Arabian Sea coastline to the Thar Desert, it combines urban sophistication with rustic charm. The bustling metropolis of Mumbai stands as India’s financial powerhouse, while Goa offers a laid-back beach vibe. Gujarat is a treasure of handicrafts, architecture, and wildlife, and Rajasthan mesmerizes with its royal palaces and desert safaris. The region is also known for its incredible cuisine, from spicy street food in Maharashtra to the sweet and tangy dishes of Gujarat. Whether you seek adventure, spirituality, or luxury, West India caters to every traveller’s interest.

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Choose West India Tour Packages
accordions.content: Diverse Experiences: From serene beaches and lush hill stations to bustling cities and ancient temples.Rich Heritage: Explore historic sites like Ajanta-Ellora Caves, Somnath Temple, and Mehrangarh Fort.Cultural Celebrations: Witness colourful festivals such as Navratri in Gujarat or Carnival in Goa.Adventure Opportunities: Enjoy trekking in the Sahyadri hills, wildlife safaris in Gir, or water sports in Goa.Gastronomic Delights: Relish unique regional cuisines — from Maharashtrian vada pav to Goan seafood curries.Convenient Connectivity: Well-developed infrastructure with airports, highways, and train routes linking all major destinations.

accordions.title: States Covered In Our West India Tour Packages
accordions.content: Maharashtra: The land of contrasts, featuring cosmopolitan Mumbai, the UNESCO-listed Ajanta and Ellora Caves, Lonavala’s misty hills, and the beaches of Alibaug.Gujarat: Known for its vibrant culture, grand temples, Rann of Kutch, and Gir National Park, the only home of the Asiatic lion.Goa: A tropical paradise of golden beaches, Portuguese heritage, and lively nightlife, perfect for both adventure seekers and leisure travellers.Rajasthan (Western Region): Offers majestic palaces, desert landscapes, camel safaris, and royal cities like Jaisalmer and Udaipur that embody India’s regal charm.

destinations.name: East India
destinations.description: East India is a captivating region known for its rich cultural heritage, historical significance, and natural diversity. Stretching from the sacred plains of Bihar to the lush coastlines of Odisha and the vibrant cityscapes of West Bengal, the region is a true blend of spirituality, art, and tradition. It’s home to iconic landmarks like the Sun Temple of Konark, the holy Bodh Gaya, and the grand Victoria Memorial in Kolkata. The landscape varies from the rolling hills of Jharkhand to the world-famous Sundarbans mangrove forest, making East India a land of contrasts and experiences.

Stretching from the sacred plains of Bihar to the lush coastlines of Odisha and the vibrant cityscapes of West Bengal, the region is a true blend of spirituality, art, and tradition. accordions.title: Titbits
accordions.content: Cultural Diversity: East India celebrates festivals such as Durga Puja, Chhath Puja, and Rath Yatra with grandeur.Cuisine: The local food varies by state—Odisha is famous for its seafood, West Bengal for sweets like Rasgulla, and Bihar for Litti Chokha.Languages: Bengali, Odia, Hindi, and Maithili are widely spoken across the region.Traditional Arts: The area is rich in crafts like Madhubani painting, Pattachitra art, and intricate terracotta work.Unique Nature: It is home to the world’s largest delta and the endangered Royal Bengal Tiger.

accordions.title: Things to Know Before Visiting East India
accordions.content: Before you travel, it’s essential to understand the region’s diverse climate—summers can be humid along the coast, while winters are mild and pleasant. The best time to visit is between October and March. Dress comfortably for sightseeing, especially when exploring temples or wildlife reserves. Be prepared for a mix of modern cities and rural landscapes, each offering a distinct cultural vibe. Local transport options like trains and auto-rickshaws are convenient for short distances, while domestic flights connect major cities. Respect local customs, especially in religious places, and always carry cash when visiting smaller towns or remote areas.

accordions.title: East India At A Glance
accordions.content: States Covered: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West BengalMajor Attractions: Bodh Gaya, Konark Temple, Puri Beach, Victoria Memorial, SundarbansCultural Highlights: Folk dances, classical music, traditional handicraftsNatural Beauty: Rivers like Ganga and Mahanadi, lush forests, and coastal plainsBest Time to Visit: October to March for festivals and comfortable weather

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Choose East India Tour Packages
accordions.content: East India tour packages are perfect for travelers who want a mix of spirituality, adventure, and cultural exploration. The region is filled with UNESCO World Heritage Sites, sacred temples, and scenic beaches. You can witness the grandeur of Durga Puja in Kolkata, visit the sacred Buddhist sites in Bihar, or unwind on Odisha’s tranquil coastline. The region also offers adventure through wildlife safaris, hill treks, and eco-tourism in mangrove areas. Affordable travel, authentic cuisine, and warm hospitality make East India an irresistible choice for every traveler.

accordions.title: The Four States of East India
accordions.content: Bihar: Known as the land of enlightenment, Bihar houses sacred Buddhist sites like Bodh Gaya and Nalanda.Jharkhand: Blessed with forests, waterfalls, and minerals, it’s ideal for eco-tourism and tribal culture exploration.Odisha: Home to the Jagannath Temple in Puri, the Sun Temple at Konark, and pristine beaches along the Bay of Bengal.West Bengal: A cultural powerhouse featuring Kolkata’s colonial charm, Darjeeling’s tea gardens, and the mystical Sundarbans.

accordions.title: Northeast India
accordions.content: Though geographically distinct, Northeast India beautifully complements East India’s charm. Comprising states like Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Sikkim, this region is renowned for its untouched landscapes, tribal cultures, and biodiversity. From the living root bridges of Meghalaya to the tea gardens of Assam and the monasteries of Sikkim, every destination tells a story of harmony between nature and tradition. The region’s friendly people, vibrant festivals, and unique cuisines make it a must-visit for travelers seeking authenticity and adventure.

destinations.name: North East
destinations.description: Northeast India, often referred to as the “Land of Seven Sisters and One Brother,” is a region celebrated for its untouched natural beauty, ethnic diversity, and rich cultural heritage. Nestled amidst the Eastern Himalayas, it comprises eight distinctive states — Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim. Each state boasts a unique identity, from misty mountains and cascading waterfalls to ancient monasteries and vibrant tribal traditions. Home to an array of wildlife sanctuaries, orchid gardens, and pristine valleys, Northeast India is a true paradise for nature lovers and adventure seekers. It offers a refreshing escape from the usual tourist trails of India, inviting travellers to experience serenity, spirituality, and unspoiled landscapes.

destinations.name: Middle East
destinations.description: The Middle East is a transcontinental region that bridges Asia, Africa, and Europe. It is typically defined by countries in Western Asia and parts of North Africa. Core Middle Eastern nations include Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Jordan, Lebanon, Israel, Syria, Iraq, Yemen, and Turkey, while Egypt is also considered part of this region due to its geographical and cultural ties. Some broader definitions may include Iran, Afghanistan, and Cyprus. Positioned between the Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf, the Middle East is one of the world’s most strategically important and historically rich areas.

accordions.title: What Areas Comprise The Middle East?
accordions.content: The Middle East is a transcontinental region that bridges Asia, Africa, and Europe. It is typically defined by countries in Western Asia and parts of North Africa. Core Middle Eastern nations include Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Jordan, Lebanon, Israel, Syria, Iraq, Yemen, and Turkey, while Egypt is also considered part of this region due to its geographical and cultural ties. Some broader definitions may include Iran, Afghanistan, and Cyprus. Positioned between the Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf, the Middle East is one of the world’s most strategically important and historically rich areas.

accordions.title: Geographical Facts About The Middle East
accordions.content: The Middle East covers diverse landscapes ranging from vast deserts to fertile valleys and rugged mountains. The Arabian Desert, stretching across Saudi Arabia, is one of the largest continuous deserts in the world. The region is also home to significant water bodies, including the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the Dead Sea (the Earth’s lowest point on land), and the Persian Gulf, which is crucial for global oil trade. Mountain ranges such as the Zagros in Iran and the Taurus in Turkey highlight the region’s varied topography. Climate-wise, the Middle East is known for its arid and semi-arid conditions, though regions like Lebanon and northern Iran experience Mediterranean and temperate climates.

accordions.title: Cultural Facts About The Middle East
accordions.content: The Middle East is often regarded as the cradle of civilization, with Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt serving as the birthplaces of agriculture, writing, and urbanization. It is also the origin of three major world religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Arabic is the most widely spoken language, though Persian (Farsi), Turkish, Hebrew, and Kurdish are also significant. Middle Eastern culture is deeply rooted in family values, hospitality, and traditions. Art forms such as intricate calligraphy, geometric patterns, and detailed architecture reflect centuries of influence. Music, poetry, and storytelling remain essential aspects of daily life.

accordions.title: Most Visited Countries In The Middle East
accordions.content: Among the most visited destinations in the Middle East are:United Arab Emirates (UAE): Known for Dubai’s modern marvels and Abu Dhabi’s cultural sites.Turkey: Famous for Istanbul’s historic blend of East and West, Cappadocia, and ancient ruins.Saudi Arabia: Increasingly popular due to religious tourism in Mecca and Medina, as well as new leisure attractions.Egypt: Renowned for its pyramids, Nile cruises, and ancient temples.Qatar and Oman: Attract visitors with luxury, heritage, and natural beauty.

accordions.title: Most Popular Cities In The Middle East
accordions.content: Travelers are often drawn to vibrant and historically significant cities such as:Dubai (UAE): A global hub for luxury, shopping, and futuristic architecture.Istanbul (Turkey): The crossroads of Europe and Asia, filled with mosques, palaces, and bazaars.Cairo (Egypt): Gateway to the pyramids and rich pharaonic heritage.Mecca and Medina (Saudi Arabia): Spiritual centers of Islam.Doha (Qatar): A rising star with modern museums and waterfront developments.Muscat (Oman): Known for its coastal beauty and traditional souks.

accordions.title: Affordable Destinations On Our Middle East Tour Packages
accordions.content: While luxury often defines the Middle East, there are also budget-friendly travel options. Jordan offers incredible sites like Petra and Wadi Rum at reasonable prices. Egypt is among the most affordable destinations, with economical Nile cruises and local markets. Turkey balances affordability with world-class attractions in Istanbul, Cappadocia, and Pamukkale. Countries such as Oman and Lebanon provide cultural and natural experiences without heavy costs compared to luxury-driven hubs like Dubai or Doha.

accordions.title: Most Visited Tourist Attractions In The Middle East
accordions.content: Some of the region’s iconic attractions include:The Pyramids of Giza (Egypt): Ancient wonders that continue to fascinate travelers.Petra (Jordan): A UNESCO World Heritage Site carved into rose-red rock.Burj Khalifa (Dubai): The tallest building in the world.Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque (Istanbul): Architectural masterpieces blending cultures.The Dead Sea (Jordan/Israel): A unique natural wonder with buoyant waters.Luxor Temples and Valley of the Kings (Egypt): Testament to ancient Egyptian civilization.

accordions.title: Most Notable Festivals In The Middle East
accordions.content: Festivals in the Middle East reflect both religious traditions and cultural heritage:Ramadan & Eid al-Fitr (Across Muslim-majority countries): A month of fasting followed by joyous celebrations.Hajj Pilgrimage (Saudi Arabia): One of the most significant religious gatherings in the world.Nowruz (Iran and Kurdish regions): Persian New Year celebrated in spring.Dubai Shopping Festival (UAE): A global shopping and entertainment extravaganza.Jerash Festival of Culture and Arts (Jordan): Showcasing music, dance, and heritage.National Day Celebrations (across Gulf nations): Marked with parades, fireworks, and cultural events.

accordions.title: Common Etiquette To Remember When Visiting Middle Eastern Countries
accordions.content: Respecting cultural norms is essential when traveling in the Middle East:Dress modestly, especially in conservative countries like Saudi Arabia, Oman, and Iran.Always ask permission before photographing people.Public displays of affection are discouraged.Removing shoes before entering a mosque or someone’s home is customary.Greetings often involve handshakes or a polite nod, but physical contact with the opposite gender may be restricted in some areas.Tipping is appreciated but not mandatory in many places.

accordions.title: Shopping
accordions.content: The Middle East is famous for its bustling souks, luxury malls, and traditional crafts. In Dubai, the Gold Souk and modern shopping centers like The Dubai Mall are must-visit spots. Istanbul’s Grand Bazaar is one of the oldest and largest markets in the world. Visitors to Egypt can explore Khan el-Khalili for spices, jewelry, and handmade items. Traditional carpets, perfumes, lanterns, and gold ornaments are among the most sought-after souvenirs. Luxury brands are also widely available in major Gulf cities, making the region a true shopping paradise.

accordions.title: Food
accordions.content: Middle Eastern cuisine is diverse, flavorful, and rooted in tradition. Staples include grilled meats, rice dishes, fresh bread, and an abundance of spices. Popular dishes include shawarma, hummus, falafel, kebabs, tabbouleh, and mansaf. Desserts such as baklava, kunafa, and dates are widely enjoyed. In the Gulf, traditional Arabic coffee and dates symbolize hospitality, while countries like Lebanon and Turkey are known for their rich culinary traditions. The region’s food culture combines communal dining, fresh ingredients, and bold flavors, making it a highlight of any visit.

destinations.name: Island
destinations.description: There are nearly 67,000 islands across the globe, with some under the ownership of specific countries while others, like Antarctica, are claimed by many nations but technically owned by none. This number is not static, as fresh islands form naturally over time while smaller uninhabited ones may vanish due to erosion.

accordions.title: About Islands in General
accordions.content: There are nearly 67,000 islands across the globe, with some under the ownership of specific countries while others, like Antarctica, are claimed by many nations but technically owned by none. This number is not static, as fresh islands form naturally over time while smaller uninhabited ones may vanish due to erosion.Greenland holds the distinction of being the largest island country in the world, although Australia—three times larger—is recognized as a continental landmass. For this reason, Australia is often called the “island continent.”The smallest inhabited island is known as Just Room Enough Island, also called Hub Island. At only 3,300 square feet, it fits a single house, a porch, and a tree. Owned by the Sizeland family, it serves as a private retreat. This unique island belongs to the Thousand Islands archipelago near New York.Nauru, covering only around 8 square miles, is the world’s smallest island country and ranks as the third smallest nation overall.Some islands remain closed to the public to safeguard the environment or preserve indigenous communities. For example, North Sentinel Island in the Andaman and Nicobar chain is home to the Sentinelese, one of the world’s oldest tribes, who have lived there for more than 60,000 years.Devon Island in Nunavut, Canada, is recognized as the world’s largest uninhabited island due to its inhospitable climate. Meanwhile, Tristan da Cunha stands as one of the most remote inhabited island groups, with over 250 families living nearly 2,800 km away from Cape Town, South Africa.

accordions.title: The Existential Threat to Islands
accordions.content: An estimated 730 million people—about 9% of the global population—live on islands. These places shelter delicate ecosystems and rare species that have survived for millennia. For instance, Iceland’s Grimsey Island is home to millions of seabirds.Islands also provide crucial insights into evolution. Madagascar, separated from other landmasses millions of years ago, forced its wildlife to adapt in unusual ways. Unique creatures like the leaf-tailed gecko evolved to camouflage perfectly against predators. Many species here exist nowhere else on Earth.Yet scientists warn that islands such as the Maldives, Fiji, Micronesia, and Tuvalu face the risk of being submerged by the century’s end. In fact, some of the Solomon Islands have already disappeared, displacing their communities. Even its famous non-stinging jellyfish population has nearly vanished.Climate change continues to accelerate this crisis. Rising sea levels and warmer oceans cause more frequent floods, coral bleaching, and marine extinctions. Corals, vital to marine ecosystems, are especially vulnerable to rising temperatures, threatening countless species that rely on them.International efforts are underway to safeguard islands, but everyday actions also matter. Choosing renewable energy, reducing waste, supporting sustainable tourism, and buying eco-friendly products can all help slow the impacts of climate change and protect these fragile lands.

accordions.content: MaldivesThe Maldives is a chain of 1,190 coral islands scattered across the Indian Ocean. Only 200 of them are inhabited, with many hosting luxurious single-resort islands. It’s a top spot for diving and snorkeling, where visitors encounter manta rays, reef sharks, clownfish, and barracuda. Popular water sports include kayaking, parasailing, surfing, jet skiing, and wakeboarding. If you are planning a holiday, consider browsing available Maldives tour packages.Sri LankaSri Lanka, formerly known as Ceylon, is an island nation near India’s southeast coast. It’s renowned for its pristine beaches, vibrant cuisine, wildlife safaris, and lush tea plantations. Highlights include Sigiriya Rock Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Uda Walawe National Park, home to elephants and deer. Relaxing Ayurveda therapies are also a major attraction. Explore available Sri Lanka tour package options for a memorable holiday.MauritiusMauritius is a tropical island in the Indian Ocean famous for its sugarcane production, pristine lagoons, and luxury resorts. It shelters unique species like Aldabra tortoises, pink pigeons, and iguanas. Beyond its biodiversity, the island offers scuba diving, underwater walking, and waterfall treks. For an adventure in paradise, check out Mauritius tour packages.Reunion IslandA French territory in the Indian Ocean, Reunion Island is known for dramatic volcanic landscapes, waterfalls, and lush forests. Visitors enjoy hiking, camping, scuba diving, and canyoning. Its forests, free from predators, make it a haven for nature enthusiasts. Look into Reunion Island tour packages for a blend of adventure and tranquility.MadagascarMadagascar, the fourth largest island, is famous for its unique biodiversity. Nearly 90% of its flora and fauna, including the baobab trees and rare lemurs, are endemic. Attractions include the Tsingy de Bemaraha Reserve and the Royal Hill of Ambohimanga. Outdoor lovers can enjoy trekking, biking, and diving. To explore further, check out Madagascar tour packages.SeychellesSeychelles, an archipelago northeast of Madagascar, is a haven for luxury seekers. Its beaches, turquoise waters, and rare species like Coco-de-Mer and Aldabra tortoises make it world-famous. With Vallee de Mai often called the “Garden of Eden,” the islands combine natural beauty with exclusivity. Explore options with Seychelles tour packages.BaliBali, Indonesia’s island province, is celebrated for its Hindu temples, cultural ceremonies, rice terraces, and beach resorts. Popular areas include Seminyak, Ubud, and Kuta. Known as the “Island of Gods,” Bali blends spirituality with adventure. Consider budget-friendly Bali tour packages for an unforgettable escape.Hong KongHong Kong, a bustling island city, is both a financial hub and a cultural hotspot. Famous for shopping, food, and Disneyland, it blends modern attractions with heritage areas like Chinatown and Little India. Discover this vibrant destination with Hong Kong tour packages.JapanJapan, an island nation with deep history, merges tradition with innovation. Highlights include cherry blossom festivals, Mount Fuji, tea ceremonies, and advanced technology. With its cultural depth and futuristic cities, Japan tour packages provide a complete experience.IndonesiaIndonesia, the largest archipelago on Earth, includes Bali, Java, and Sumatra. It’s celebrated for temples, tropical forests, wildlife, and a rich cuisine featuring satay and nasi goreng. To explore its diverse landscapes, browse Indonesia tour packages.SingaporeSingapore is a modern island nation known for cleanliness, multicultural neighborhoods, and iconic landmarks like Marina Bay Sands and Gardens by the Bay. With vibrant shopping and heritage sites, Singapore tour package options are perfect for short vacations.PhilippinesThe Philippines consists of over 7,000 islands offering natural wonders like Palawan, Boracay, and Banaue rice terraces. Its heritage combines Spanish, American, and Asian influences. For beaches, culture, and history, check Philippines tour packages.TaiwanTaiwan blends modernity with rich traditions. Explore its charm with Taiwan tour packages.GreenlandGreenland is part of Denmark and known for its glaciers, fjords, and wildlife, including polar bears and whales. The northern lights are its most famous attraction. For an Arctic adventure, check Greenland tour packages.IcelandIceland is known for geysers, volcanoes, glaciers, and the northern lights. Recognized for safety and happiness, Iceland tour packages are ideal for explorers.IrelandThe Republic of Ireland offers castles, green landscapes, and heritage sites like the Giant’s Causeway. With its history and scenic charm, it’s a must-visit destination. Browse Ireland tour package options to explore more.United KingdomThe UK consists of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. Visitors can discover both bustling cities and tranquil countryside with UK tour packages.FijiFiji is made up of 333 islands with pristine beaches, colorful reefs, and friendly culture. destinations.name: Europe
destinations.description: Europe is one of the most diverse continents in the world, blending ancient history, modern innovations, and breathtaking landscapes. Before visiting, travelers should be aware of a few key points:

accordions.title: Things To Know Before Visiting Europe
accordions.content: Europe is one of the most diverse continents in the world, blending ancient history, modern innovations, and breathtaking landscapes. Before visiting, travelers should be aware of a few key points:Visa Requirements: Most Indian travelers require a Schengen visa to visit multiple European countries.Currency: The Euro is widely used, but some nations like Switzerland (Swiss Franc) and the UK (British Pound) have their own.Languages: English is commonly spoken, but each country has its own national language.Transport: Europe is well-connected with high-speed trains, budget airlines, and extensive road networks.Cultural Etiquette: Customs vary across regions, so learning basic greetings in the local language is always appreciated.

accordions.title: Europe At A Glance
accordions.content: Continent Size: Second smallest in area but rich in cultural and geographical diversity.Countries: 50 nations, including popular destinations like France, Italy, and Spain.History: Cradle of Western civilisation, home to the Renaissance, Enlightenment, and Industrial Revolution.Geography: Features snowy Alps, sunny Mediterranean coastlines, vast plains, and historic rivers like the Danube and Rhine.Tourism: Europe welcomes millions of international travelers each year for art, history, cuisine, and natural beauty.

accordions.title: Top Reasons To Visit Europe
accordions.content: Rich Cultural Heritage – From Greek ruins to Gothic cathedrals and Renaissance art.World-Class Cuisine – French pastries, Italian pasta, Spanish tapas, and Swiss chocolates.Scenic Beauty – Snowy mountains, charming villages, and Mediterranean beaches.Festivals & Events – Oktoberfest in Germany, La Tomatina in Spain, and Christmas markets across Central Europe.Shopping Paradise – Luxury fashion in Paris, flea markets in Amsterdam, and traditional crafts in Prague.

accordions.title: 5 Most Visited Countries In Europe By Indians

accordions.title: 5 Least Visited Countries In Europe You Must Visit

accordions.title: 5 Budget Destinations To Visit From India
accordions.content: Hungary – Affordable stays, thermal baths, and Budapest nightlife.Poland – Kraków and Warsaw offer history at budget-friendly prices.Czech Republic – Prague’s castles, bridges, and vibrant culture.Portugal – Sunny beaches, seafood, and inexpensive wine.Greece – Santorini sunsets and Athens’ ruins without breaking the bank.

accordions.title: Things To Remember When Travelling To Europe
accordions.content: Always carry travel insurance.Book train and flight tickets in advance for better deals.Check SIM card or roaming plans for connectivity.Keep some cash for small shops and rural areas.Respect local customs, especially in religious sites.

accordions.title: Best Time To Visit Europe From India

accordions.title: Things To Do In Europe

destinations.name: Asia
destinations.description: Asia spans 44.58 million km², making it the largest continent on Earth.

accordions.title: Geography Facts About Asia
accordions.content: Asia spans 44.58 million km², making it the largest continent on Earth.It includes 49 countries, spanning multiple climate zones from polar in Siberia to tropical in Southeast Asia.It contains the world’s highest point, Mount Everest, and the lowest land point, the Dead Sea.Major mountain ranges like the Himalayas, deserts like the Gobi, and rivers like the Yangtze define its diverse terrain.Asia borders three major oceans – the Pacific, Arctic, and Indian.

accordions.title: Cultural Facts About Asia
accordions.content: Asia is home to more than 2,300 languages and countless dialects.It is the birthplace of major religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, Judaism, and Christianity.Traditional arts like Chinese calligraphy, Indian classical dance, and Japanese tea ceremonies reflect deep cultural values.Family and community play a central role in most Asian societies.Modern Asia blends ancient traditions with contemporary lifestyles, especially in cities like Seoul and Tokyo.

accordions.title: Most Visited Country In Asia (2023)
accordions.content: In 2023, Thailand emerged as the most visited country in Asia, welcoming over 28 million international tourists. Visitors flocked to Bangkok, Phuket, and Chiang Mai for their rich heritage, street food, scenic beaches, and vibrant nightlife. The country’s relaxed visa policies and reputation for hospitality also contributed to its tourism boom.

accordions.title: Least Visited Countries In Asia (2023)
accordions.content: Some of Asia's least visited nations in 2023 include:Bhutan – Due to its "High Value, Low Impact" tourism policy and daily tourist fee.Timor-Leste – A hidden gem with limited infrastructure and low international awareness.Turkmenistan – With stringent visa requirements and controlled tourism.Despite low numbers, these countries offer unique cultural and ecological experiences.

accordions.title: Most Popular Cities In Asia
accordions.content: Bangkok, Thailand – Known for its street markets and temples.Tokyo, Japan – A futuristic blend of technology and tradition.Dubai, UAE – Iconic for luxury shopping, architecture, and global events.Singapore – Clean, efficient, and a melting pot of cultures.Seoul, South Korea – Famous for K-pop, tech, and vibrant street food.These cities are major tourism and business hubs, welcoming millions of visitors annually

accordions.title: Most Visited Tourist Attractions In Asia
accordions.content: Great Wall of China, China – Over 10 million annual visitors.Taj Mahal, India – A UNESCO World Heritage site and symbol of love.Mount Fuji, Japan – Iconic peak and pilgrimage site.Angkor Wat, Cambodia – The world’s largest religious monument.Petronas Towers, Malaysia – Architectural marvel in Kuala Lumpur.These sites draw millions for their historical, cultural, and natural significance.

accordions.title: Common Etiquette To Remember When Visiting Asian Countries
accordions.content: Respect elders and authority figures.Remove shoes before entering homes or temples.Dress modestly, especially at religious sites.Use both hands when giving or receiving items.Avoid public displays of affection in more conservative countries.Never point your feet at someone or religious objects.Etiquette may vary, but mutual respect is a universal expectation.

accordions.title: Common Must-Try Delicacies In Asia
accordions.content: Sushi (Japan) – Fresh seafood paired with vinegared rice.Pho (Vietnam) – Aromatic noodle soup with beef or chicken.Dim Sum (China) – Bite-sized steamed and fried snacks.Biryani (India) – Spiced rice with meat or vegetables.Pad Thai (Thailand) – Stir-fried rice noodles with peanuts and lime.Kebabs (Middle East) – Grilled meat on skewers with spices.Each dish tells a story of tradition, geography, and local ingredients.

packages.title: Romantic Journeys with Sri Lanka Honeymoon Tour Package
packages.description: After breakfast, head out to explore Kandy City. This medieval city has several cultural and historical attractions, including the Temple of the Tooth Relic, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.Begin your Kandy city tour with a visit to the Sri Dalada Maligawa, or the Temple of the Tooth Relic, which is believed to hold a tooth of the Buddha. Every year, Buddhists celebrate the Kandy Esala Perahara, an annual procession in which the sacred tooth is paraded on a majestic elephant adorned with a majestic golden casket.Other attractions in Kandy include the Royal Botanical Gardens, the Bahirawakanda Temple, Kandy Lake, and the Ceylon Tea Museum. The Royal Botanical Garden was founded in 1371 and was once only allowed to royalty. The garden has thousands of flora and fauna, including orchids, bamboo, weeping figs, and an extensive spice garden. The Botanical Garden is also home to the exclusive coco de mer, the world’s largest seed, popularly called double coconut.Spend the night in Kandy.

package_itineraries.title: Arrival in Srinagar & Sunset Shikara on Dal Lake
package_itineraries.description: Meet and greet at Srinagar Airport by our representative. Transfer to your luxury houseboat. Evening relaxing 1-hour shikara ride on Dal Lake passing floating gardens and lotus blossoms.
package_itineraries.activities: Airport pickup, Houseboat check-in, Dal Lake Shikara ride

package_itineraries.title: Mughal Gardens & Historic Srinagar Sightseeing
package_itineraries.description: Visit the world-renowned Mughal terraced gardens: Nishat Bagh (Garden of Pleasure) and Shalimar Bagh (Abode of Love), followed by Chashme Shahi and Shankaracharya Hill temple.
package_itineraries.activities: Sightseeing of Mughal Gardens, Old Srinagar heritage walk

package_itineraries.title: Gulmarg Meadow of Flowers & Gondola Ride
package_itineraries.description: Scenic drive to Gulmarg. Board the famous Gulmarg Gondola up to Kongdoori Phase 1 (elev. 10,000 ft). Enjoy snow views and optional skiing or snowmobiling.
package_itineraries.activities: Gondola ride, snow play, alpine photography

package_itineraries.title: Pahalgam Valley of Shepherds & Lidder River
package_itineraries.description: Drive along saffron fields of Pampore to reach Pahalgam. Visit scenic Betaab Valley where Bollywood movies were filmed, and stroll beside the turquoise Lidder river.
package_itineraries.activities: Saffron field stop, Betaab Valley, Lidder river walk

package_itineraries.title: Aru Valley & Kashmiri Handicrafts Shopping
package_itineraries.description: Explore the unspoiled alpine meadows of Aru Valley. Return to Srinagar for an afternoon visiting authentic Pashmina shawl looms and walnut woodcarving workshops.
package_itineraries.activities: Aru Valley exploration, artisan craft workshops, Wazwan feast

package_itineraries.title: Departure with Cherished Himalayan Memories
package_itineraries.description: After a leisurely breakfast overlooking the water, transfer to Srinagar International Airport for your flight home with unforgettable memories.

package_itineraries.title: Arrival in Male & Seaplane Transfer to Paradise Island
package_itineraries.description: Land at Velana International Airport and board your scenic seaplane flight over sparkling atolls. Check in to your luxury Beach Villa. Welcome tropical cocktail & dinner.
package_itineraries.activities: Seaplane transfer, resort welcome, beach sunset walk

package_itineraries.title: House Reef Snorkeling & Sunset Dolphin Cruise
package_itineraries.description: Swim in warm crystal waters alongside sea turtles and colorful reef fish. In the late afternoon, embark on a traditional Maldivian Dhoni cruise to spot playful spinner dolphins.
package_itineraries.activities: Guided reef snorkeling, sunset dolphin cruise

package_itineraries.title: Water Villa Check-In & Overwater Spa Therapy
package_itineraries.description: Transfer to your iconic Overwater Villa with glass floor panels and direct sea stairs. Enjoy an afternoon couple signature aromatherapeutic massage at the overwater spa.
package_itineraries.activities: Water villa transition, couple spa ritual, private sundeck relaxing

package_itineraries.title: Kayak Safari & Candlelight Beach Dinner
package_itineraries.description: Paddle transparent kayaks across calm lagoons. In the evening, enjoy a private 5-course romantic candlelight dinner on the secluded beach under starlit skies.
package_itineraries.activities: Clear kayak safari, private candlelight dinner

package_itineraries.title: Farewell Maldives & Seaplane Return
package_itineraries.description: Enjoy a leisurely breakfast over the lagoon before your seaplane return transfer to Male for your flight home.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrive in Bali
package_itineraries.description: Upon reaching Bali, you’ll be greeted at the airport and transferred to your hotel. The rest of the day is free to unwind, enjoy the surroundings, or explore nearby attractions at your leisure.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Celuk Village – Mas Village – Elephant Cave – Kintamani – Ubud Village Tour
package_itineraries.description: Start the day at Celuk Village, renowned for its intricate gold and silver jewellery crafted by local artisans. Continue to Mas Village, where skilled craftsmen create elaborate wooden carvings. Visit the historic Elephant Cave (Goa Gajah), an important Hindu archaeological site. The journey then leads to Tirta Empul Temple, where holy spring water is believed to hold purifying powers. Later, admire the volcanic beauty of Mount Batur and Lake Batur in Kintamani. Before heading back, explore Ubud Market for traditional Balinese crafts and souvenirs.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Tanjung Benoa Beach
package_itineraries.description: Enjoy a fun-filled day at Tanjung Benoa Beach, a hub for exciting water sports like parasailing, jet skiing, and banana boat rides. In the afternoon, relax with a rejuvenating spa session that will leave you refreshed and re-energized. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Depart from Bali
package_itineraries.description: Check out from your hotel and transfer to the airport for your return flight, carrying with you the memories of a splendid Bali experience.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrive at Dubai – Miracle Garden - Dhow Cruise
package_itineraries.description: Arrive in Dubai and check into your hotel. Start your trip with Miracle Garden, spread over 72,000 sq. meters with over 150 million flowers. In the evening, enjoy a Dhow Cruise with dinner and entertainment. Return to the hotel for rest.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Burj Khalifa – Dubai Creek – Dubai Mall - Jumeirah Beach
package_itineraries.description: Visit the Burj Khalifa and explore its observation decks. Continue to Dubai Creek for a boat ride, then enjoy retail therapy at Dubai Mall. End the day at Jumeirah Beach.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Desert Safari
package_itineraries.description: Spend the day in the desert, enjoying dune bashing, camel rides, and sand skiing. Watch live shows, taste delicious BBQ dinner, and rest under the desert stars before returning to your hotel.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Sharjah - Al Corniche Beach - Sharjah Natural History Museum and Desert Park
package_itineraries.description: Head to Sharjah and check into your hotel. Visit Al Corniche Beach, followed by the Sharjah Natural History Museum and Desert Park, where you can also interact with farm animals.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Mleiha Archaeological Centre - Sharjah Aquarium - Al Noor Island
package_itineraries.description: Begin with Mleiha Archaeological Centre to explore history and nature. Visit Sharjah Aquarium, home to 250 species of marine life. End your day at Al Noor Island, featuring a Butterfly House, café, playground, and modern art.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Depart from Sharjah
package_itineraries.description: Check out from the hotel and transfer to the airport for your departure.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Zurich – Lucerne
package_itineraries.description: Arrive in Zurich and travel to Lucerne. Explore the Old Town, Chapel Bridge, and Lion Monument, or enjoy a boat ride on Lake Lucerne. Overnight in Lucerne.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Lucerne – Mount Titlis
package_itineraries.description: Travel to Engelberg and ride the Rotair cable car to Mount Titlis , where snow awaits year-round. Admire panoramic alpine views before returning to Lucerne.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Lucerne – Interlaken
package_itineraries.description: Board a train to Interlaken. Spend the day exploring or trying adventure activities like paragliding. Evening strolls along Interlaken’s streets are highly recommended.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Jungfraujoch Excursion
package_itineraries.description: Travel to Jungfraujoch , the “Top of Europe,” and explore the Ice Palace and Sphinx Observatory. Return to Interlaken in the evening.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Interlaken – Bern City Tour
package_itineraries.description: Adventure seekers may try bungee jumping or a helicopter ride. Later, take a train to Bern for a city tour featuring the Rose Garden, Clock Tower, and Bern Cathedral before returning to Interlaken.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Interlaken – Zurich
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, travel to Zurich. Visit the Rhine Falls and explore Zurich’s vibrant old streets, markets, and museums.

package_itineraries.title: Day 7: Departure
package_itineraries.description: Check out and transfer to Zurich Airport for your departure.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrival in Kochi
package_itineraries.description: Arrive in Kochi and check in to your hotel. Begin sightseeing with a visit to Mattancherry Palace, Hill Palace Museum, Paradesi Synagogue, St. Francis Church, and the famous Chinese fishing nets. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Kochi to Alleppey
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, travel to Alleppey, known for its backwaters, lagoons, and beaches. Check in to your hotel and enjoy lunch. Stroll along Alleppey Beach in the evening before returning for the night.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Alleppey to Kumarakom
package_itineraries.description: Post breakfast, drive to Kumarakom and board a houseboat at 12:30 PM. Cruise along Vembanad Lake while enjoying local cuisine prepared onboard. Relax amidst the serene surroundings and spend the night on the houseboat.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Departure from Kochi
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, check out from the houseboat and drive to Kochi Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Delhi – Shimla
package_itineraries.description: Arrive at Delhi airport, where you’ll be assisted with your transfer to Shimla. The scenic 8-hour drive showcases the majestic Shivalik mountain ranges. After checking into the hotel, explore the nearby surroundings or rest.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Shimla City Tour
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, set out for local sightseeing. Visit Christ Church, Viceregal Lodge, Shri Hanuman Temple, Kali Bari Temple, Annadale Ground, and Green Valley. Spend the evening at Mall Road, enjoying shopping and dining before returning to your hotel for the night.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Shimla – Manali
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, drive to Manali. The 8-hour journey offers spectacular landscapes, mountain valleys, and lush forests. Upon arrival, check in at the hotel and spend the night in Manali.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Manali
package_itineraries.description: Today, explore Manali’s major attractions including the Hadimba Devi Temple, Tibetan monasteries, and the hot springs of Vashisht Kund. Later, browse through the local markets for handicrafts before returning to your hotel.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Snow Point Excursion
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, head for an excursion to the nearby snow points—Kothi, Gulaba, Marhi, and the iconic Rohtang Pass. Later, enjoy Solang Valley, famous for adventure sports and breathtaking landscapes. Return to Manali for an overnight stay

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Manali – Chandigarh
package_itineraries.description: Leave Manali after breakfast and travel to Chandigarh, known for its urban planning and modern architecture. Visit Rock Garden, Rose Garden, and Sukhna Lake. Stay overnight in Chandigarh.

package_itineraries.title: Day 7: Chandigarh – Delhi
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, check out and return to Delhi. Proceed to the airport or railway station for your onward journey.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrival in Hanoi
package_itineraries.description: Arrive in Hanoi and begin a city tour featuring the Temple of Literature , Ba Dinh Square , and the Old Quarter by cyclo, including a visit to Ngoc Son Temple . Overnight in Hanoi.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Hanoi - Tam Coc - Hoa Lu - Hanoi
package_itineraries.description: Head to Ninh Binh for a boat trip through the Tam Coc caves and a visit to the ancient capital Hoa Lu . See temples dedicated to King Dinh and King Le. Lunch included. Return to Hanoi for the night.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Hanoi to Halong
package_itineraries.description: Travel to Halong Bay , a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site. Cruise among limestone cliffs, visit caves, and enjoy swimming or kayaking. Dinner and overnight on board.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Halong – Hanoi – Saigon
package_itineraries.description: Cruise back to Halong Wharf, passing by Cock-Fighting Rock, Sail Island, and other famous islets. Return to Hanoi and fly to Saigon . Overnight in Saigon.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Saigon – Mekong Delta – Saigon
package_itineraries.description: Explore the Mekong Delta with boat trips, island visits, local factory stops, honey tea tasting, and a horse-cart ride. Visit Vinh Trang Pagoda before returning to Saigon. Overnight stay.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Saigon – Cu Chi Tunnels
package_itineraries.description: Visit the Cu Chi Tunnels , a wartime relic. In the evening, explore Saigon’s shopping spots such as Ben Thanh Market, Saigon Square, or Diamond Plaza. Overnight in Saigon.

package_itineraries.title: Day 7: Depart Saigon
package_itineraries.description: Breakfast at the hotel before your airport transfer.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrival in London
package_itineraries.description: Arrive at Heathrow, transfer to your hotel, and check in. Spend the day at leisure near your hotel. Overnight in London.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: London City Tour
package_itineraries.description: Visit UNESCO sites like the Tower of London, Westminster Palace, Greenwich, and Royal Botanical Gardens. Other stops include Buckingham Palace, London Eye, London Bridge, British Museum, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Big Ben, Hyde Park, Natural History Museum, Trafalgar Square, Kensington Palace, Borough Market, and London Aquarium.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: London to Paris
package_itineraries.description: Travel to Paris on the Eurostar (approx. 2.5 hours). On arrival, transfer to your hotel and explore nearby areas in the evening.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Paris City Tour
package_itineraries.description: Discover the Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame, Arc de Triomphe, Luxembourg Gardens, Pantheon, and Palace of Versailles. The guided tour offers audio in multiple languages and includes lunch.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Disneyland Paris
package_itineraries.description: Travel 32 km outside Paris to Disneyland, with rides, shows, and shopping. Return to your hotel in the evening.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Departure from Paris
package_itineraries.description: Check out and transfer to the airport for your return flight.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrive in Goa
package_itineraries.description: Upon your arrival, our representatives will welcome you and escort you to your hotel. After check-in, freshen up and take some time to relax. Spend the remainder of the day exploring romantic local attractions before returning for a restful night.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: South Goa
package_itineraries.description: After a hearty breakfast, head out to experience the peaceful charm of South Goa. Visit the revered Shree Mangueshi Temple and the iconic churches of Old Goa. End your day at Dona Paula, where you can indulge in sunbathing or adventurous water activities like jet skiing, kayaking, and scuba diving.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: North Goa
package_itineraries.description: Post breakfast, embark on a North Goa tour filled with scenic beaches and lively vibes. Enjoy dolphin watching and explore the historic Aguada Fort, a magnificent 17th-century Portuguese structure. Return to your hotel and unwind.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Depart Goa
package_itineraries.description: Enjoy breakfast at leisure, soak in your last moments in Goa, and then check out from the hotel. Proceed to the airport or railway station for your return journey home.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrive in Jammu
package_itineraries.description: Upon arriving at Jammu Airport, you will be greeted by your tour representative, who will assist you on your drive to Katra. The journey takes about one and a half hours and is filled with stunning mountain views. Check into your hotel and spend the rest of the day exploring the surroundings. Overnight stay in Katra.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Katra – Vaishno Devi
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, set out for a spiritual journey to the Vaishno Devi Temple, a revered 700-year-old shrine devoted to Maa Shakti. After completing your darshan, return to the hotel for an overnight stay in Katra.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Katra – Pahalgam
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, drive to Pahalgam, a tranquil hill station adorned with verdant meadows and glistening rivers. Upon arrival, check into your hotel and enjoy exploring the charming surroundings. Spend the night in Pahalgam.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Pahalgam – Gulmarg
package_itineraries.description: In the morning, explore local attractions in Pahalgam, such as Mamaleshwar Temple, Chandanwari, Wadiy e Hajan, and the sacred Amarnath Cave Temple. Later, proceed to Gulmarg, known for its scenic gondola rides and alpine beauty. Visit Strawberry Valley, Afarwat, and Drung Waterfall before retiring for the night in Gulmarg.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Gulmarg – Srinagar
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, head to Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir. Visit Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Garden, Pari Mahal, the Tulip Garden, Hari Parbat, and Dal Lake. Enjoy a serene houseboat stay overnight in Srinagar.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Srinagar
package_itineraries.description: Today, explore the places you missed yesterday. Take a boat ride across Dal Lake, visit the Floating Gardens, Lal Chowk, and Sinthan Top, or simply unwind amid the natural beauty. Overnight stay in Srinagar.

package_itineraries.title: Day 7: Srinagar
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, enjoy a relaxed day. You can visit Sri Shankaracharya Temple, go shopping for souvenirs, or simply relax in your houseboat with a warm cup of Kashmiri kahwa. Stay overnight in Srinagar.

package_itineraries.title: Day 8: Depart Srinagar
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, check out and proceed to the airport to board your flight home, carrying wonderful memories of your Kashmir journey.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrival in Vancouver
package_itineraries.description: Arrive at Vancouver International Airport, collect your rental vehicle, and drive to your hotel. In the evening, enjoy the exhilarating Fly Over Canada 4D experience—soar across Canada's diverse landscapes with immersive visuals and special effects. Relax overnight at your Vancouver hotel.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: Vancouver Exploration
package_itineraries.description: Today begins with a visit to Vancouver’s top attractions. Cross the iconic Lions Gate Bridge and explore the Capilano Salmon Hatchery before arriving at the Capilano Suspension Bridge Park. Stroll along the thrilling Cliff Walk and immerse yourself in the Treetops Adventure. Continue your day with a scenic ride up Grouse Mountain on the Skyride. Enjoy activities such as the Lumberjack Show, the Peak Chairlift, wildlife encounters, and panoramic views from the Eye of the Wind. In the evening, unwind in downtown Vancouver—shop on Robson Street, visit Stanley Park, or explore the historic Gastown district. Overnight in Vancouver.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: Vancouver to Victoria
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, head to Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal for a 90-minute ferry ride across the Strait of Georgia to Swartz Bay. Visit the world-famous Butchart Gardens, known for its immaculate floral displays. Then, explore Victoria’s Inner Harbour, steeped in British charm. Overnight stay in Victoria.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Victoria to Whistler
package_itineraries.description: Start your day with an included Whale Watching Tour. Spot orcas, seals, and marine birds in their natural habitat. Later, take the ferry from Nanaimo to Horseshoe Bay and enjoy a scenic drive along the Sea-to-Sky Highway to Whistler. Stop at Shannon Falls and soak in views of rugged mountains and glacial fjords. Overnight in Whistler.

package_itineraries.title: Day 5: Whistler Adventure
package_itineraries.description: Explore Whistler Village and savour a local breakfast. Enjoy shopping, dining, or outdoor cafés before boarding the Peak-2-Peak Gondola—an engineering marvel offering breathtaking views. Optional adventures include ATV tours, bungee jumping, or a paddling trip across Alta Lake and the River of Golden Dreams. Stay overnight in Whistler.

package_itineraries.title: Day 6: Whistler to Kamloops
package_itineraries.description: Drive to Kamloops, where dramatic desert plateaus meet lush valleys. Enjoy scenic views of Kamloops Lake and the Thompson River. Experience the peaceful rhythm of small-town life and settle in for an overnight stay.

package_itineraries.title: Day 7: Kamloops to Jasper
package_itineraries.description: Travel north along the Thompson River, passing through Yellowhead Pass into Jasper National Park. Admire the alpine lakes, towering peaks, and chance wildlife sightings like elk. End your day in the picturesque mountain town of Jasper. Overnight at a Jasper hotel.

package_itineraries.title: Day 8: Explore Jasper National Park
package_itineraries.description: Enjoy a day exploring Jasper's natural beauty. Visit Maligne Canyon and take a boat cruise on Maligne Lake to view Spirit Island. Optional activities include visiting Miette Hot Springs, white water rafting, or the Jasper SkyTram. Overnight stay in Jasper.

package_itineraries.title: Day 9: Jasper to Lake Louise via Columbia Icefields
package_itineraries.description: Today, journey along the Icefields Parkway—one of the most scenic drives in the world. Stop at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre for the Glacier Adventure and Glacier Skywalk. En route to Lake Louise, pass scenic spots like Peyto Lake and Bow Lake. Spend the night at a hotel near the tranquil turquoise waters of Lake Louise.

package_itineraries.title: Day 10: Lake Louise to Banff
package_itineraries.description: Begin the day exploring Lake Louise with optional activities such as hiking to Lake Agnes, kayaking, or visiting the Lake Louise Gondola. Later, head to Banff, a vibrant alpine town. Check into your hotel and enjoy Banff Avenue’s quaint shops and restaurants. Overnight in Banff.

package_itineraries.title: Day 11: Banff Sightseeing
package_itineraries.description: Explore Banff’s majestic surroundings. Visit Bow Falls, Surprise Corner, Hoodoos, and take a Lake Minnewanka Cruise. Ascend Sulphur Mountain via Banff Gondola for panoramic views. In the afternoon, explore the trails or stroll through town. Overnight in Banff.

package_itineraries.title: Day 12: Banff to Calgary
package_itineraries.description: Drive from Banff to Calgary. Once in the city, check into your hotel and enjoy free time exploring urban attractions or relaxing. Overnight stay in Calgary.

package_itineraries.title: Day 13: Departure from Calgary
package_itineraries.description: Spend the morning exploring Calgary’s top sites like Heritage Park, Canada Olympic Park, or the Calgary Tower. Return your rental vehicle at Calgary Airport and catch your return flight or continue your journey elsewhere.

package_itineraries.title: Day 1: Arrival in San Francisco
package_itineraries.description: Your journey begins as you arrive in the beautiful city of San Francisco—often compared to global icons like Paris or London for its charm and cultural richness. The city's famous rolling hills provide sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay. With its diverse neighborhoods, vibrant nightlife, and proximity to Silicon Valley, San Francisco welcomes you with open arms. After arrival, you’ll check in at your hotel and spend the night in this iconic city.

package_itineraries.title: Day 2: San Francisco City Exploration
package_itineraries.description: Start your day with a delightful breakfast before setting out on a full-day tour of San Francisco. Visit the Golden Gate Bridge, known for its towering structure and spectacular views. Explore landmarks like Twin Peaks, the famous Lombard Street, Nob Hill, Union Square, Civic Center, and the Palace of Fine Arts. Take in the lively vibe at Fisherman’s Wharf, hop on a historic cable car, and browse shops at Pier 39. Return to your hotel for an overnight stay in San Francisco.

package_itineraries.title: Day 3: San Francisco to Las Vegas
package_itineraries.description: After breakfast, catch your flight to Las Vegas—America’s glittering city of entertainment. Upon arrival, transfer to your hotel and prepare for an exciting evening. Enjoy a panoramic city tour featuring dazzling sights like the Bellagio Fountains, Treasure Island's pirate show, the towering Stratosphere, Downtown Vegas, and the famous Fremont Street Experience—a light and sound show unlike any other. Overnight stay at a hotel in Las Vegas.

package_itineraries.title: Day 4: Optional Grand Canyon Tour
package_itineraries.description: Begin the day with breakfast and choose how you'd like to spend it.
